title: From a Young Palace Maid to a Great General
author: Tang Bo
synopsis:
The story takes place over a decade surrounding the An Lushan Rebellion.

County Magistrate Wei Zhuoqing has a beautiful 16-year-old daughter named Ziyun, who is unfortunately coveted by the local bully, Yang, who intends to take her as a concubine.

Having practiced martial arts with her uncle since childhood, Ziyun refuses to become a plaything for the old tyrant. Because the bully is a relative of Yang Guozhong, the Wei family is no match for the Yang family.

Ziyun realizes she must save herself, so she enters the palace as a maid to escape the bully's clutches. In the palace, she is relegated to menial, grueling tasks like scrubbing waste buckets, suffering immensely.

To keep the frontier soldiers warm, Emperor Tang Xuanzong orders the women of the six palaces to sew cotton battle robes.

Ziyun sews an extra-large robe and stitches a poem she wrote into the collar, the gist of which is...

chapters.title: The Wei Family's Daughter Comes of Age
chapters.content:
At the beginning of the Kaiyuan Era of the Great Tang Empire, the country was strong and the people were wealthy. All industries flourished, and the entire nation basked in a scene of prosperity and vitality.

In a small courtyard on the outskirts of the imperial capital, Chang'an, lived Magistrate Wei Zhuoqing and his family.

Although Magistrate Wei was a law-abiding but unsuccessful minor official, he had a daughter who was as beautiful as a fairy, rebellious in nature, and daring beyond measure.

This daughter would bring a profound impact on both her family and the imperial court, yet her story remains little known and was never passed down.

In Chang'an, a minor county magistrate was nothing more than a sesame-seed-sized official. It was much like Beijing today, if you accidentally let out a foul-smelling fart, you would likely knock out a whole row of mid-level bureaucrats.

A small, insignificant official, without backing from higher-ups or money to bribe superiors and grease the wheels, was often met with the cold shoulders and bullying of the powerful and wealthy.

Magistrate Wei did not know how to network or flatter; he lived honestly, worked diligently, and followed the law. As a result, he never gained the appreciation of his superiors. Despite being filled with knowledge, he had no place to put his talents to use.

He had served as a magistrate for many years, feeling deeply frustrated and unfulfilled. His wife, Madam Zhou, had borne him a daughter and a son. The eldest, Ziyun, was 12 years old when Consort Yang first gained the Emperor's favor.

The younger son, Zizhu, was four years younger than his sister.

With his career in ruins, Magistrate Wei poured his energy into raising his children. He not only sent them to private school early but also personally taught them the ways of the sages.

However, Ziyun was rebellious by nature; she had little heart for reading but an excess of passion for martial arts.

Madam Zhou’s younger brother, Zhou Xing, was a martial arts graduate who had once served as a chief instructor for the Imperial Guard. Having offended his superiors and been pushed out, he was idle at home and often visited his sister’s house.

Ziyun often pestered her uncle to teach her boxing and martial arts. At first, Zhou Xing only taught his niece some self-defense techniques, never intending to teach her real combat skills.

To his surprise, Ziyun practiced with extraordinary dedication and progressed rapidly. Soon, simple boxing and kicking were no longer enough to satisfy her, and she forced her uncle to teach her how to wield blades and spears.

Madam Zhou was displeased when she saw this and scolded Zhou Xing: "Is this how you act as an uncle? She is a girl! Instead of teaching her poetry and etiquette, you spend all day having her brandish weapons. Does she look like a young lady at all?"

"Sister, I am only teaching her a few moves for self-defense; it won't hinder her study of poetry and etiquette," Zhou Xing defended himself.

But by then, it was too late to stop Ziyun. By the time she was fourteen or fifteen, she could wield various weapons with ease and was proficient in combat, horseback riding, and archery. She had sparred with many boys her age and defeated them all.

Her uncle had to admit that she was a genius at martial arts.

She was a tomboy by nature; she neither liked feminine attire nor was she skilled at applying makeup. By the time she turned 15, she had blossomed into a stunning beauty, a real head-turner.

This worried Madam Wei greatly. If she continued like this, what man would dare marry her? From then on, she restricted Ziyun from going out, forbade her uncle from teaching her martial arts, and forced her to stay home to learn needlework.

Even though Ziyun was a thousand times unwilling, she could not defy her mother’s threat to die, so she had to settle down and learn embroidery.

Because she was naturally intelligent and dexterous, she made rapid progress in her needlework. Before long, she had mastered all kinds of floral patterns and embroidery.

When her mother saw the needlework she produced, she couldn't believe it was the work of the tomboy who spent all day brandishing weapons.

Madam Wei thought to herself: "What a clever pair of hands this child has. Fortunately, they weren't ruined by her uncle."

By the time Ziyun turned 16, her beauty became even more breathtaking. Colleagues of Magistrate Wei and wealthy families often sent matchmakers to propose marriage, but Ziyun seemed unwilling to marry so young.

When matchmakers or suitors came, she would either refuse to see them or give them a cold look.

If she absolutely had to meet them, she would perform a set of boxing moves or brandish a staff or spear right in front of them, scaring them so much that they never dared to return.

Good wine doesn't fear a deep alley, and a beauty cannot be hidden forever. News of the beautiful maiden in Magistrate Wei’s home spread like wildfire, eventually reaching the ears of the local bully, Yang Guoguang.

This Yang Guoguang was over 50, short and stout, with a fat head, big ears, a face full of flab, a snub nose, buck teeth, and a mouth full of black teeth. Everyone who saw him felt disgusted.

He was originally a street ruffian and a local menace. He colluded with petty thieves, relying on violence, extortion, and bullying to survive and dominate the neighborhood.

Ever since Consort Yang gained favor, the Yang family had risen to power. The bully Yang was a distant relative of Yang Guozhong. Relying on the influence of the Yang clan, he gathered a group of thugs to engage in fraud, monopolize markets, and use force to carve out his own territory, becoming a major local tyrant.

Throughout history, it has been said that ugly men have stronger sexual desires than average men. Thus, they are particularly lecherous. Ancient people blamed this on character, while modern medicine attributes it to physiological causes.

Although the bully Yang already had a house full of wives and concubines, he was never satisfied. He not only frequented brothels but also sent people out to find young beauties; he was particularly fond of those just budding into womanhood.

Hearing that Magistrate Wei had a daughter as beautiful as a fairy, he drooled with desire, thinking of her day and night until he lost his appetite.

He sent matchmakers to Magistrate Wei’s home several times, wanting the man’s precious daughter to be his concubine, but Magistrate Wei politely refused, and the matchmakers returned empty-handed.

Seeing that a mere county magistrate dared not give him face, the bully Yang was furious and decided he had to teach the Wei family a lesson.

However, no matter how small a magistrate is, he is still an official of the imperial court.

No matter how powerful the Yang family was, they couldn't openly kidnap the magistrate’s daughter. He had to find some trouble for Magistrate Wei, make his life a living hell, and let him know the power of the Yang family. Eventually, he would force them to deliver the precious daughter to his doorstep.

He handed this task to his confidant, Master Zhang, a glib and cunning slave.

Master Zhang had connections with the government above and colluded with local thugs and ruffians below. Whatever the government couldn't handle, he would find these thugs to do, and there was nothing these thugs couldn't accomplish.

However, to deal with a small magistrate, Master Zhang’s best method was to find Magistrate Wei’s superior, Lord Li.

This Lord Li was a relative of Emperor Xuanzong; by rank, he was the Emperor’s nephew.

Lord Li was a notoriously dim-witted official. He was unlearned and lacked the ability to distinguish right from wrong. Not only was he muddled, but he was also arrogant and stubborn, daring to make arbitrary decisions on any matter. He had created many unjust cases and was called a "pig official" by the common people.

Master Zhang knew this well. Therefore, he intended to exploit Lord Li’s arrogance and stupidity.

After careful planning, Master Zhang took several petitions he had personally forged and drafted to the Li estate.

When Lord Li read them, he saw that these petitions accused Magistrate Wei of corruption, perverting the law, and disregarding human life.

In fact, these cases were based on old cases handled by Lord Li himself, which he had long since forgotten.

After reading the petitions, Lord Li flew into a rage and roared: "How can there be such a corrupt official? Once I investigate the truth, I will not show mercy!"

Master Zhang flattered him: "My Lord has always been wise, decisive, and impartial. Please investigate, my Lord. However..."

Master Zhang hesitated. Lord Li had a fiery temper and asked: "However what? Speak!"

"My Lord, I only fear that news might leak out. If word gets out and this corrupt magistrate runs away, the case will be difficult to handle. It would be better to detain him first."

Master Zhang finished his thought.

"That is easy," Lord Li said decisively. "He wants to run? No way! Throw him into the prefectural prison first. Even if he grew wings, he wouldn't be able to fly away. After I investigate the truth, I will punish him."

Lord Li immediately ordered Magistrate Wei to be thrown into the prefectural prison for no reason and notified his family to bring him food and clothing.

Master Zhang handled everything with precision. He had already bribed the jailer and instructed him on how to treat Magistrate Wei.

When Madam Zhou, Magistrate Wei’s wife, received the news that her husband had been imprisoned, she was terrified.

She came from a scholarly family and, hearing the news, was both shocked and frightened. She had never dealt with jailers and dared not go to the prison alone, so she immediately asked her brother, Zhou Xing, to go with her to visit the prison.

Zhou Xing was experienced and felt that his brother-in-law had always been law-abiding and had never done anything illegal, so he asked his sister: "What crime did my brother-in-law commit?"

"The messenger didn't say. I asked, but they wouldn't tell me. They just told me to bring food and clothes. Won't we know everything once we see him? I don't dare go alone, please come with me." Madam Wei truly knew nothing.

"Fine, you prepare the food and clothes, and I will go with you." Zhou Xing knew his sister was timid; besides, it was indeed inappropriate for a woman to go to a prison alone.

The siblings arrived at the prefectural prison with the clothes and food.

After the duty jailer verified their identities, he said to them: "Go inside, turn right, and it’s the third cell after the corner. Go ahead."

The siblings found the third cell. It was large and held over a dozen prisoners. Magistrate Wei was curled up in a corner, and one look at him showed he was suffering.

The jailer shouted: "Magistrate Wei, your family is here to bring you things!"

Magistrate Wei immediately crawled up from the floor and ran to the wooden bars. Madam Wei rushed over, crying, and passed the food through the gaps in the bars.

Zhou Xing also passed the clothes through.

Magistrate Wei leaned close to Zhou Xing’s ear and whispered: "Get me moved to another cell quickly; they want to kill me."

Zhou Xing nodded.

At this moment, the jailer shouted: "Speak quickly if you have something to say! The prison is not a place for chatting. Visiting hours are over!"

After coming out, Zhou Xing searched for connections and used silver and copper coins to bribe the head jailer to move his brother-in-law to a single cell to ensure his safety.

In fact, this was all Master Zhang’s plan.

Zhou Xing had a friend who was a relative of the head jailer, and the money had been paid. He knew very well that people often died in prison for no reason, and the safety of prisoners was not guaranteed.

The head jailer, having received the benefits from Zhou Xing, said: "I can guarantee Magistrate Wei’s safety, but if you want to save him, you must go find Master Zhang." Jailers throughout history were never kind; they took bribes from both sides.

Once Zhou Xing heard this, he knew what the lawsuit against his brother-in-law was really about. To save him, Ziyun would have to become the bully Yang’s concubine.

Wasn't this throwing Ziyun into a pit of fire? Given her personality, it was absolutely impossible for her to become the bully Yang’s concubine.

If she were pushed too far, she would truly take a desperate path. Zhou Xing knew this better than anyone.

In this way, he could neither save his brother-in-law nor protect Ziyun. If things went wrong, both lives would be lost. What could he do?

Furthermore, Magistrate Wei was an honest official with no savings, land, or property to sell. By this point, the family’s money was already gone.

In such matters, every step required money; without it, one could not move an inch. Zhou Xing himself was a down-and-out instructor who was usually spendthrift and had no savings; he often came to his sister’s house to sponge off meals, so he couldn't come up with money to handle the situation.

Madam Wei was frantic. Should she save her husband or her daughter?

Saving both was impossible. The siblings discussed it repeatedly and finally decided to save the husband first.

The siblings’ plan was this: agree to the marriage verbally, and once Magistrate Wei was released from prison, they would find a way to deal with Ziyun’s situation.

But they couldn't let Ziyun know for the time being; if she found out, she would cause an even bigger scene that would be impossible to control.

Everything would wait until Magistrate Wei was rescued. The siblings begged for help everywhere and scraped together some copper coins to buy gifts to see Master Zhang.

When Master Zhang saw the siblings bringing gifts, he knew his little scheme had succeeded. He was both smug and happy, his face full of smiles, and he spoke very kindly.

After accepting their gifts, he said with a grin: "Don't be so polite in the future; it's too vulgar. Once your daughter arrives at Magistrate Yang’s house, she will enjoy endless glory and wealth. Even Magistrate Wei will rise in his career. He is still just a small magistrate, right?"

Master Zhang asked a question he already knew the answer to.

At this, Madam Wei couldn't help but shed tears.

Seeing this, Master Zhang asked in feigned surprise: "Madam, why are you sad? Has your daughter been wronged?"

Zhou Xing hurriedly explained: "My brother-in-law is still in the prefectural prison. My sister is just worried, that’s why she’s crying."

"What?" Master Zhang pretended not to know and exclaimed: "Who locked our in-law in prison? What did he do?"

Zhou Xing replied: "We don't know either. He was locked up yesterday. Please, Master Zhang, find a way to save him. Everyone knows my brother-in-law is an honest official."

"Are you sure our in-law is in the prefectural prison?" Master Zhang asked again, knowing full well.

"We are sure. He is in the prefectural prison. My sister and I just brought him food and clothes," Zhou Xing said.

"Audacious!" Master Zhang widened his eyes and shouted: "Who dares to be so unreasonable to Magistrate Yang’s future father-in-law? Since our in-law is in trouble and has come to me, I will report this to Magistrate Yang."

"Thank you, Master Zhang!" Madam Wei and Zhou Xing immediately bowed and kowtowed to him.

"You don't need to be so polite. From now on, we are one family. Who would dare to be so unreasonable to you again?

"Although this is the prosperous Tang Dynasty and the world belongs to the Li family, the real power inside and outside the palace is in the hands of our Yang family. Take this Yang family token to the prefectural prison and tell the jailer to treat Magistrate Wei well, arrange for him to stay in a preferential single cell, and ensure his safety."

At this point, Master Zhang said to Madam Wei in a terrifying tone: "I hear the prison is very chaotic, and prisoners often die for no reason."

After saying this, he added: "You don't need to worry about anything else. Just take good care of your daughter. After Magistrate Wei comes out, we will choose an auspicious day and use an eight-bearer sedan chair to marry her over. Go back and wait for the news."

After Master Zhang finished speaking, he told his servants to see the siblings out.

Master Zhang handled this matter quite smoothly. He understood that he couldn't let Magistrate Wei marry off his daughter while in prison; that would be unlucky.

He wasn't afraid that the Wei family would go back on their word after Magistrate Wei was released; after all, the power of life and death was in their hands.

If Magistrate Wei reneged, they could just arrest him again and throw him back into prison. He was confident in this.

He wanted his master to be happy about taking a concubine, and he wanted Magistrate Wei to be happy about marrying off his daughter. Both sides would be happy, and everyone would be satisfied. Master Zhang did things cleanly and efficiently.

The next day, Magistrate Wei was released without a scratch.

Everyone in the Wei family knew that Magistrate Wei’s imprisonment was orchestrated by Master Zhang; he was the one who arrested him and the one who released him.

But even knowing that, what could they do? Magistrate Wei was a low-ranking official with no power and no money; he could only endure the bullying and exploitation of the tyrant.

Master Zhang felt that his plan was foolproof and finally set his mind at ease.

This time, he had not only handled a great happy event for his master but would also gain many benefits from it.

In the old days, masters, stewards, and accountants all fattened themselves while working for their masters.

chapters.title: The Only Way Out
chapters.content:
After Zhou Xing and his sister brought Magistrate Wei home, they recounted the entire ordeal of how his brother-in-law had been thrown into prison. Magistrate Wei sighed and said, "It is obvious. This is all the work of the tyrant Yang. He is the one pulling the strings behind the scenes, both for the arrests and the releases."

"If," Zhou Xing said, "we do not satisfy the tyrant Yang's desires and let Ziyun become a concubine to this old scoundrel, the next person to suffer might not just be you, brother-in-law. It is possible that our entire family will meet a tragic end."

"Indeed." Magistrate Wei knew all too well what kind of person the tyrant Yang was. He said helplessly, "Knowing full well that it is a pit of fire, how can I watch my own daughter jump into it?"

However, the family could not come up with any good solution, so they had no choice but to tell Ziyun the truth. Given her strong and rebellious nature, how could she be willing to become a concubine to such an inhumane tyrant?

But if she refused, it would not just be her own misfortune; her parents, uncle, and younger brother would not be able to escape the clutches of the tyrant Yang.

After much thought, Ziyun could not find a way out.

Finally, she thought of death.

If she died, everything would be over. But if she died, would the tyrant Yang let her father and family go?

That was hard to say. If the tyrant Yang did not achieve his goal, he would not spare her father and family. Sacrificing herself would not save them. Ziyun could not commit such a foolish act.

Marry him? That would be worse than death. She checked the almanac; there were only five days left until the next auspicious date.

Ziyun had only five days to decide her fate. What could she do? What good options did a sixteen-year-old girl have? Should she marry him as a stalling tactic for the safety of her parents and family, and then plan accordingly?

With her martial arts skills, killing a man over fifty would not be difficult. Ziyun thought to herself, "Even if I die, I will drag this old beast down with me!"

In the end, she made up her mind: she would fight this old beast to the death, and they would perish together.

Her parents and uncle were waiting for her answer. She approached them with great composure and said, "Father, Mother, Uncle, do not worry about me anymore. Just agree to his terms."

Upon hearing this, her mother rushed over and hugged her: "My child, you have been wronged..." She was unable to continue, sobbing uncontrollably.

Magistrate Wei and his brother-in-law could only sigh. With a few days left, her mother tearfully began preparing for her daughter's wedding.

Although Magistrate Wei knew the situation was irreversible, he did not give up hope completely. There were still a few days left to run around, pull strings, and ask for help. He had to try his best if there was even a glimmer of hope.

At this critical moment, an imperial decree arrived from the capital: the annual imperial selection of concubines had begun.

Coincidentally, the official in charge of the selection for this region was an old acquaintance of Magistrate Wei, a fellow scholar who had passed the imperial examinations in the same year, named Wu Jie.

Magistrate Wu had studied hard for the exams alongside Magistrate Wei, and they had forged a deep friendship.

After Magistrate Wu finished discussing official business, Magistrate Wei told him about being thrown into prison by Yang Guoguang.

Magistrate Wu was shocked and asked, "Magistrate Wei, what are your plans?"

"I ask Magistrate Wu to give me an idea. How can I avoid offending the tyrant Yang while saving my daughter from this sea of misery and protecting the lives of my entire family? As for whether I can continue as a magistrate, that no longer matters." Wei Zhuoqing was truly at his wit's end.

Magistrate Wu thought for a moment and said to Magistrate Wei, "This Yang Guoguang is notorious. I have long heard of his evil reputation, and dealing with him is difficult. I have suffered at his hands before. Alas, the Yang family's influence is too great; there is nothing to be done about him."

"My family and I cannot think of any good way either. It is truly driving us to death!" Magistrate Wei looked miserable. He had only heard of people being driven to death, but now it had fallen upon him.

"I have endured Yang Guoguang until now, and I am filled with rage! I will certainly help you with this matter. I will ask you a few questions, and you must answer them truthfully, agreed?"

"Very well," Magistrate Wei said. "I will answer truthfully. Please, ask."

"First question: Has Yang Guoguang come to your home to propose marriage?"

Magistrate Wei replied, "He has, but I refused him. That is why they threw me into prison on those trumped-up charges."

"You did well to refuse!" Magistrate Wu said. "Second question: Did they send any betrothal gifts afterward?"

Magistrate Wei replied, "No."

"Good. Third question: Have you agreed to betroth your daughter to him? If you did agree, did you say it to his parents or to him personally?"

Magistrate Wei replied, "I said it to his secretary. I have never met Yang Guoguang himself, let alone his parents."

"Oh, that makes it easier. Your daughter can still be saved."

After asking the three questions, Magistrate Wu had a plan in mind.

Magistrate Wei, however, did not understand and asked, "Magistrate Wu, you know that my mind has never been as sharp as yours. I don't understand; please enlighten me."

"Brother, you are too modest. There is a saying: 'Success depends on human effort.' This is true for everything. You are an honest official, a good man. When a good man encounters difficulties, he must be helped. Heaven has shown mercy, and I am the person sent by Heaven to help you."

Hearing that Magistrate Wu was willing to help him get through this, Magistrate Wei wanted to kowtow to him immediately.

Just as he was about to kneel, Magistrate Wu helped him up: "This must not be. We are fellow scholars and close friends; this is absolutely unnecessary!"

"If you help me this time, you will be the great benefactor of the Wei family!" One can understand the feelings of a person who, at their wit's end, meets someone willing to pull them out of the abyss.

"Brother, don't say that; I don't deserve it. However, I will tell you how to save your daughter." Having said this, Magistrate Wu looked around.

Magistrate Wei said, "There are no outsiders here. I have sent the bailiffs away; they are not in the room. You can speak freely."

"The imperial selection does not compete with the common people for wives, nor can it seize the wives of the common people. Therefore, the rules for the imperial selection are very strict. Beauties who are already betrothed or engaged cannot be selected.

"What is considered betrothed or engaged? The palace has clear regulations: if a girl's parents have arranged a marriage, she is considered engaged and cannot be selected as a concubine;

"If a matchmaker has made a proposal, the girl's parents have agreed, and they have accepted the betrothal gifts, she is considered engaged and cannot be selected;

"If the girl's parents have promised their daughter to the man himself or his parents, it is called a betrothal, and she cannot be selected.

"Your daughter has neither been promised to Yang Guoguang nor is she engaged, so she can be selected as a concubine.

"What your wife said to the secretary, Zhang, does not count. If your wife had said the same thing to Yang Guoguang himself or his parents, your daughter would be considered betrothed to him, and the imperial selection would not take her.

"Therefore, I have decided to select your daughter as a concubine. No matter how powerful the Yang family is, they would not dare to compete with the Emperor for a concubine, would they?"

Magistrate Wei suddenly realized the truth and nodded deeply. This was indeed an excellent way to save his precious daughter from the fire.

Magistrate Wu added, "I want to see how capable Yang Guoguang is at snatching your daughter away from the imperial selection. If he truly dares to compete with the Emperor for a concubine, he will not have many days left before his head is chopped off."

"He wouldn't dare, even if he were given the guts of a dog! These corrupt officials only know how to bully the common people and low-ranking officials like us who have no power," Magistrate Wei said resentfully.

"As the saying goes, a dog will jump over a wall when desperate. Yang Guoguang will not give up easily since he didn't get the person he dreams of, and he will surely take his anger out on you."

"Then what should I do?" Magistrate Wei was now completely at a loss.

"To prevent Yang Guoguang from causing trouble for you and your family, go to him immediately and explain. Tell him that I, Magistrate Wu, have been sent by the imperial court to select concubines for the Emperor. Selecting your daughter is my duty and mission. Let's see what he says."

Magistrate Wu was on imperial business and was not afraid of the tyrant Yang; he dared to challenge him.

Magistrate Wei asked with lingering fear, "The tyrant Yang is ruthless and capable of any evil. Aren't you afraid he will poison you?"

"I am not afraid. He and I have a history; he knows I am targeting him, and he knows I am not afraid of him. He has Yang Guozhong as his backer, but I also have people in the capital. With me here, he will not trouble you for the time being."

Magistrate Wu was genuinely trying to save Magistrate Wei.

Magistrate Wei thanked him profusely.

That very day, he went to tell Secretary Zhang the truth.

Secretary Zhang was shocked. How could this duck that was already cooked fly away? How could he explain this to his master?

He asked Magistrate Wei, "Didn't you say that Ziyun was already betrothed to Master Yang?"

"I did," Magistrate Wei said, "but Magistrate Wu asked me if she was betrothed to Master Yang himself or to his parents. I said she was betrothed to Secretary Zhang."

"Are you stupid?" Secretary Zhang immediately flared up. "You... couldn't you have just said she was betrothed to Master Yang? Why did you say she was betrothed to me?" Secretary Zhang was so anxious that he could barely speak clearly.

"I have never even seen what Master Yang looks like, so how could I lie? Avoiding the imperial selection is a capital crime; I could only tell the truth," Magistrate Wei said with a bitter face.

"What is the name of that selection official, and what is his background?" Secretary Zhang asked.

"His name is Wu Jie," Magistrate Wei said. "I don't know what his background is, but in any case, I dare not defy the imperial decree. I have just submitted my daughter's name; whether she is selected or not, I do not know."

"She hasn't been taken away yet, right?" Secretary Zhang asked.

"No, today is registration, and tomorrow is the preliminary selection," Magistrate Wei said.

"Don't do anything rash," Secretary Zhang said. "Wait for my news. I am going to report this to Master Yang immediately."

Secretary Zhang hurried back to Yang Guoguang's mansion and reported everything Magistrate Wei had said.

The tyrant Yang became nervous as soon as he heard that Wu Jie was an imperial official in charge of the selection.

He had a grudge against Wu Jie and knew that he would surely use public office to settle a private score and would never let him get this beauty easily.

However, he could not think of a good way to communicate with Magistrate Wu. He knew that being tough with Magistrate Wu would be useless, as Magistrate Wu was not afraid of him. At this moment, the tyrant Yang was also at a loss.

Snatching a woman from the hands of the tyrant Yang was like pulling teeth from a tiger's mouth; the tyrant would not let it go.

On the surface, there was no fault to be found with Magistrate Wu, and there was no immediate danger to the Wei family.

Secretary Zhang knew his master best; he would be unable to eat or sleep until he got Ziyun, and he knew this matter was far from over.

As the most loyal dog raised by the tyrant, he had to share his master's worries. He had to find a way to make Ziyun fail the selection. As long as she didn't enter the palace, wouldn't she still be a piece of fresh meat in his master's bowl?

Secretary Zhang reported his plan to the tyrant Yang.

"Exactly!" The tyrant Yang was very excited after hearing the plan. "Do as you suggested. Use as much silver as you need. As long as I can get my little beauty, money is no problem.

"If you get that little beauty for me, you will have performed a great service, and I will reward you handsomely!"

"Thank you, Master. Should I have the steward go with me? Two heads are better than one." Secretary Zhang wanted to use this opportunity to siphon off more silver from the accounts, and he said this specifically to avoid suspicion.

"In matters like this, if it goes well, it's fine; if it goes poorly, heads will roll! You should go alone. More people mean more danger! It is hard to get a girl selected, but easy to get her disqualified. Don't be afraid to spend money. Get it done for me, and don't embarrass me."

Yang Guoguang believed that money could make the devil turn the mill, and that there was nothing in this world that couldn't be done with money. This played right into Secretary Zhang's scheme.

"Master is absolutely right. More people mean more danger. I will handle this myself. This Magistrate Wu has a grudge against you, but he has no grudge against money, right? Don't worry, Master, I will definitely bring your sweetheart into your warm bed!"

"Hahaha!" The tyrant Yang laughed loudly. "There is nothing in this world that our secretary cannot handle!"

Secretary Zhang hosted a dinner in the name of the tyrant Yang to entertain Magistrate Wu. When Magistrate Wu received the invitation, he actually went.

The dinner was held at the famous Hongyun Restaurant in Chang'an. The table was full of local dignitaries who had come to show their support for Yang Guoguang. However, Yang Guoguang himself did not attend, fearing that they might fall out again and nothing would be accomplished. It was safer for Secretary Zhang to handle it.

Magistrate Wu really wanted to meet this evil enemy once more. After many years, he wanted to see what kind of face he had now.

Magistrate Wu was slightly disappointed that the tyrant Yang did not show his face.

At the table, Magistrate Wu appeared very easygoing. His capacity for alcohol was astonishing; he refused no one who offered him a drink.

Everyone who drinks knows that words spoken and promises made at the dinner table do not count.

After the banquet, Secretary Zhang personally escorted Magistrate Wu to the inn.

"Magistrate Wu, I have a request." In Magistrate Wu's room, Secretary Zhang revealed the purpose of the banquet.

"Secretary Zhang is Master Yang's favorite; what could Master Yang not accomplish? Hahaha!" Magistrate Wu did not say he would or would not do it, waiting to see what Secretary Zhang would say next.

Seeing that Magistrate Wu did not refuse, Secretary Zhang knew it was time to act.

He took out five gold ingots and pushed them toward Magistrate Wu: "I know that you are here on imperial orders to select concubines. This is fifty taels of gold. As long as you let Wei Ziyun fail the selection, you will have done Master Yang a great favor."

Magistrate Wu accepted the gold with a smile. After putting the ingots away, he said to Secretary Zhang, "Go back and tell your master: getting someone selected is difficult, but getting someone disqualified is not difficult at all."

After Secretary Zhang returned, he relayed Magistrate Wu's words to Yang Guoguang and claimed he had given Magistrate Wu sixty taels of gold.

In reality, Secretary Zhang had withdrawn sixty-five taels from the accounts. He spent five taels on the banquet and other expenses, and pocketed the extra ten taels for himself.

Thinking the matter was settled, he was shocked the next day to hear that not only had Wei Ziyun been selected as a concubine, but she had already entered the palace.

Only then did the tyrant Yang realize that Magistrate Wu had used this to take revenge on him, taking his gold without doing the job. He had no place to seek justice and had suffered a major, silent loss.

After Magistrate Wu sent Wei Ziyun into the palace, he said to Wei Zhuoqing, "I know exactly what kind of person Yang Guoguang is. Since he didn't achieve his goal, he will not let this go. If you don't leave this place, you will be harmed sooner or later. It would be better to resign from your post, find a place far from Chang'an, buy a house and land, and spend your remaining years in peace."

"To tell you the truth, you have done me such a great favor, but I don't even have the money to treat you to a drink, let alone buy a house and land," Magistrate Wei said, truly being an honest official with nothing to his name.

Magistrate Wu "slapped" fifty taels of gold onto the table, giving Magistrate Wei a big fright.

Magistrate Wei knew Magistrate Wu was not a corrupt official and asked, "Where did you get so much gold? It couldn't be...?"

Seeing that the gold had frightened Magistrate Wei, Magistrate Wu explained, "This gold is not mine," and then told Magistrate Wei the whole story of how he had obtained the gold.

Finally, he said to Magistrate Wei, "While I am still here, take your family and leave immediately. Go as far as you can. Find a place where no one can find you, and spend your remaining years in peace and happiness."

Magistrate Wei accepted the gold and thanked Magistrate Wu profusely.

Magistrate Wu said, "Save your thanks until you are safe. Leave immediately, the sooner the better! If you don't leave, you will be a trouble for me!"

Magistrate Wei understood the gravity of the situation and left quietly with his entire family that very day.

chapters.title: Hardships in the Palace (1)
chapters.content:
The bully Yang, accustomed to being arrogant and overbearing, was furious. Not only had he failed to obtain the girl Ziyun, but he had also lost a large sum of money.

After summoning his incompetent advisor, Master Zhang, and berating him mercilessly, the two of them vented their rage on Magistrate Wei.

"Take some men at once and drag that damned Wei Zhuoqing here to me!" the bully Yang roared.

What he did not expect was that when Master Zhang arrived at the Wei residence with his servants, the house was already empty; the entire family had long since vanished.

They went to the county office, where the yamen runners told Master Zhang that Magistrate Wei had resigned and left, and that a new magistrate would be arriving shortly.

Only then did it dawn on Master Zhang that this had been a trap set for him by Lord Wu in collusion with Magistrate Wei, and he had walked right into it.

However, he could not admit that he had been duped. If his master knew he was this foolish, he would not only be berated to death, but his master would also suspect his competence was declining, leading to a loss of trust, or worse, the loss of his current position.

He could only claim that Lord Wu was settling a private grudge and had played them for fools.

When the bully Yang confirmed that he had been toyed with by Lord Wu and Magistrate Wei, he felt an immense sense of humiliation. If he did not avenge this insult and wash away this shame, he would have no face to be reincarnated as a human in his next life.

But how could it be easy to retaliate against Lord Wu? He was an official sent by imperial decree to conduct the selection of palace maids. Throughout the entire process, he had committed no irregularities and given no cause for criticism. Moreover, Lord Wu’s backing at court was not to be underestimated; one could not act rashly.

For the time being, the bully Yang had no way to deal with Lord Wu and had to swallow his pride. He could only wait for an opportunity. In officialdom, things are unpredictable; who knows when someone might fall and end up in another’s hands?

He hoped that one day Lord Wu would fall into his grasp, so he could settle old and new scores together.

Wei Zhuoqing, carrying the fifty gold ingots given to him by Lord Wu, led his entire family to seek refuge with Yan Gaoqing, who was then the Prefect of Changshan.

Yan Gaoqing was a close friend of Wei Zhuoqing, and the great calligrapher Yan Zhenqing was Yan Gaoqing’s cousin.

Wei Zhuoqing was a great admirer of Yan Zhenqing’s calligraphy and had once asked Yan Gaoqing to introduce him to study under the master, a wish that had remained unfulfilled for various reasons.

There was certainly a reason for him to bring his family to seek refuge now.

Yan Gaoqing asked Wei Zhuoqing, "How could you bear to leave the blessed land of the imperial capital and travel a thousand miles to seek me out?"

Wei Zhuoqing recounted the events in detail, finally sighing, "I have reached a dead end. If you can provide a place for me to stay, my entire family will forever remember your great kindness."

"We call each other brothers; we share both blessings and hardships. That you would come to me when in trouble shows your trust and respect for me, how could I refuse to help?

"Besides, Yang Guozhong holds the reins of government, and his family members have risen to power like dogs and chickens ascending to heaven. They are everywhere, seizing property and committing all kinds of evil. The public resentment is immense; it is good that you have stayed far away from him.

"Rest assured, your family can live here in peace. No one will be able to find you."

Yan Gaoqing, a man of integrity and righteousness, immediately agreed to Wei Zhuoqing’s request.

Wei Zhuoqing settled down in Changshan, buying a house and land. Before long, he began to have dealings with Yan Zhenqing.

The girl Ziyun had participated in the selection to escape the clutches of the bully Yang; she had no genuine desire to be a palace maid.

However, once she entered the palace gates, she was no longer in control of her own fate. After a series of screenings and assessments, Ziyun was kept as a palace maid in the Xingqing Palace, one of the six palaces.

There were three thousand palace maids in the entire palace, and several hundred in the Xingqing Palace alone. These hundreds of maids were divided into various ranks.

The work assigned to these maids differed according to their rank.

Generally, a newly arrived maid who had no one to look after her and whose family had not used money to grease the wheels could only be assigned to the lowest level, performing the dirtiest and most exhausting manual labor.

Especially for a "double-void" maid like Ziyun, one who had neither money to bribe officials nor any connections to speak for her, she could only become a menial servant.

Although all three thousand beauties of the six palaces were intended for the Emperor, in reality, very few ever saw him.

In the palace, the work performed by maids of different ranks varied.

Ziyun and two other newly arrived maids were assigned to scrub the night-soil buckets.

These two maids were the same age as Ziyun; one was named Zhang Xiaocui, and the other was Liang Wenjuan.

While the three girls were not exactly pampered princesses at home, they were the beloved darlings of their parents. How could they endure such dirty and exhausting work?

Yet, if they refused or did a poor job, they would be punished with the cane.

The head maid in charge of the three was named Yan Jiao, a cruel and ruthless old woman.

When she first entered the palace, she had hoped to receive the Emperor’s favor. But half a lifetime had passed, and she hadn't even caught a glimpse of the Emperor’s shadow.

Old and bitter, she had become psychologically twisted, finding pleasure in punishing the young maids.

On the first day of work, Yan Jiao led the three maids to a well and said, "The water in this well is bitter; it is used specifically for scrubbing the night-soil buckets."

The three girls looked around and saw stagnant water everywhere. The ground around the well was covered in filth, and they couldn't help but feel nauseated.

Yan Jiao observed their expressions, noting them well, and knew how to deal with these three weak women.

She pointed with the bamboo cane in her hand toward a patch of open ground not far away. "Do you see those wooden stakes and the buckets hanging on them?"

The three saw a large area of stakes, each with a bucket inverted upon it; some were still dripping with foul water.

They understood: the purpose was to drain the buckets.

What shocked them was how there could be so many buckets.

Yan Jiao, seeing their thoughts, said, "There are 300 buckets in total. You three must finish scrubbing them all within one day, and they must be clean. I will inspect them one by one. If I find even one that isn't clean, that’s ten strokes of the cane!"

The three girls looked at the mountain of buckets, their faces full of distress.

Naturally, their expressions were caught by Yan Jiao.

She sneered, "Whether you work together or separately, each of you must scrub 100 buckets a day!

"If you don't finish, or if they aren't clean, or if I smell anything, watch out for your skin! The cane is fair to everyone; I will show no mercy!"

With that, she brandished the bamboo cane like a warrior’s blade.

The cane was three feet long and an inch wide, its surface polished to a shine, one could tell at a glance it had been used to beat many people.

Liang Wenjuan and Zhang Xiaocui hurriedly replied timidly, "We understand."

Ziyun remained silent.

Seeing Ziyun’s silence, Yan Jiao glared at her fiercely and took note.

"Good that you understand!" Yan Jiao said, pointing to a pile of sundries. "The bamboo brushes, bristle brushes, and water scoops are all there. If you run out, tell me. If a bucket is leaking, tell me too. Do you hear me?"

Liang Wenjuan and Zhang Xiaocui immediately replied, "We hear you!"

Ziyun still did not speak.

Yan Jiao glared at her again and continued, "If a bucket leaks and you don't tell me, you'll get the cane."

After saying this, she brandished her cane again, making it whistle through the air.

Again, Liang Wenjuan and Zhang Xiaocui replied, "We understand!"

Finally, Yan Jiao said sternly, "Stay here and do your work honestly. Don't cause any trouble, and get the idea of seeing the Emperor out of your heads as soon as possible!"

"If we aren't to see the Emperor, why were we selected to enter the palace?" Ziyun asked coldly.

Yan Jiao had been tolerating Ziyun for a long time; her hands were itching, and she had wanted to lash out at this rebellious girl several times.

However, she didn't know the background of these three newcomers and wasn't sure who they might be connected to.

Based on her years of experience, Ziyun seemed to have some sort of backing. If she beat the wrong person, she would be in serious trouble.

That was why the cane hadn't landed yet. But in her heart, she thought, Just you wait, girl. I'll make you pay. I'm keeping a tally of your lashes for now!

"Heh heh!" Yan Jiao sneered. "The girls who are lucky enough to see the Emperor aren't scrubbing buckets here. Get that thought out of your minds!

"I have been in the palace for 30 years, and I haven't even seen the Emperor's shadow. Do you really think the Emperor would come to a filthy place like this?!"

"Then are we to scrub buckets here for the rest of our lives?" Zhang Xiaocui, seeing that Ziyun had spoken, also dared to ask.

"Well, I can tell you this: you only do this work for one year. Next year, when new people arrive, you won't have to do these dirty, tiring jobs."

Changing the subject, she said to the three girls, "The premise is that you must work hard and keep me satisfied. Otherwise, you'll just die here!"

"Thank you for your guidance, Head Maid," the three girls replied in unison.

Head Maid Yan finally showed a faint smile, pointing to some clothes hanging on a wall. "Those are left by your predecessors. Change into them to work. If you like cleanliness, wash them; they'll dry in half a day. Go change!"

Once the three girls had changed into their work clothes, Head Maid Yan said, "I will teach you how to work for one day. Listen carefully; I will say this only once, not a second time. Do you hear me?"

"We hear you!"

"The first thing is drawing water from the well," Head Maid Yan said.

The three girls had never drawn water from a well at home. They stood by the well, staring at it, not knowing how to begin.

Head Maid Yan saw that none of them knew how to draw water. She didn't get angry, but instead patiently demonstrated how to draw water from the well.

After teaching them, she asked, "Do you know how now?"

The three girls replied, "We do."

"Each of you, draw a bucket of water for me," Head Maid Yan ordered.

The three girls began to draw water from the well with wooden buckets.

Ziyun had practiced martial arts and was quick to learn. She was the first to successfully draw a bucket of water and wash the well platform clean.

Liang Wenjuan was also quite nimble; she drew the second bucket and washed the platform again.

Zhang Xiaocui was not so lucky. After much effort, she only managed to draw half a bucket of water.

Head Maid Yan immediately turned hostile. She pointed her bamboo cane at Xiaocui’s nose and roared, "I've never seen anyone as stupid as you! I think you're asking for a beating. Lift your skirt and bend over!"

Xiaocui hadn't expected the Head Maid to turn on her so quickly and so viciously. She was terrified and didn't know what to do. Before she could react, the Head Maid’s cane had already struck her face.

In an instant, a wide, bloody welt appeared on Xiaocui’s face.

Ziyun and Wenjuan were terrified to see the Head Maid strike so ruthlessly.

After the strike, she said to Xiaocui, "Lift your skirt and bend over higher!"

Xiaocui, ignoring the pain in her face and fearing another blow to it, immediately lifted her skirt and bent over, exposing her fair, tender buttocks.

Head Maid Yan did not strike her buttocks immediately.

Instead, she said to the other two girls, "In the future, when I tell you to lift your skirts and bend over, this is what I mean. Otherwise, I'll beat your faces to a pulp. Did you see clearly?"

Ziyun and Wenjuan said loudly, "We saw clearly!"

"Good," Head Maid Yan said coldly. "As long as you are obedient, I won't disfigure you. If the Emperor happens to see you, perhaps there is still hope for you to become a consort."

With that, she told Ziyun and Wenjuan, "Stand with Xiaocui, lift your skirts, and bend over!"

Although Ziyun and Wenjuan had done nothing wrong, they had no choice but to obey. They stood in a row with Xiaocui, lifting their skirts and bending over.

Ziyun was very indignant, but this was her first day in the palace, and she knew nothing of the place. She dared not act rashly, silently warning herself: Endure, endure, endure!

"If you make a mistake, you must accept punishment," Head Maid Yan said with a gloomy face. "This is Xiaocui's first time, so I won't punish her too severely; this is just a reminder for you all." With that, she struck Xiaocui’s buttocks with the cane.

Poor Xiaocui let out a cry, and a long, bloody welt appeared on her fair skin.

"Remember this: from now on, the starting punishment for a mistake is ten strokes. Today, I let Xiaocui have a taste of it. Don't make mistakes in the future, do you understand?"

Xiaocui, fearing more beatings, immediately said, "I understand!"

Head Maid Yan brandished the cane but did not strike Xiaocui again.

"Good that you understand. I'll spare you for today, but the remaining eight strokes are on your tab. If you make another mistake, it will be eighteen strokes. You two were just collateral today..."

Before she could finish, the cart delivering the night-soil buckets arrived.

Head Maid Yan said to the three girls, "Go and unload all the buckets from the cart and dump out the waste.

"Then, take the clean, dried buckets from the stakes and put them on the cart. After that, you will scrub the buckets. I advise you three to work together; it's faster and easier. If you don't finish before dark, you don't eat. Get to work, I'm leaving."

Head Maid Yan left.

Ziyun saw that there were 15 carts, each with 20 buckets, all parked in the courtyard.

The eunuch who delivered the buckets parked the carts in the courtyard and left.

When Head Maid Yan left, she closed the gate. In the vast courtyard, only the three young girls and the carts of buckets remained.

Xiaocui hadn't dared to cry while the Head Maid was there, but once she left, she burst into tears; the welt on her face was burning with pain.

Ziyun said to her with concern, "Don't cry; the tears will make it sting more."

Hearing this, Xiaocui realized it was true and stopped crying.

Ziyun checked the wounds on Xiaocui’s face and buttocks. Fortunately, the skin hadn't broken. She said, "It's fine, it will heal in a couple of days."

"How are we supposed to scrub so many buckets?" Wenjuan asked.

"Have neither of you ever done manual labor at home?" Ziyun asked.

"No," the two girls replied in unison.

"Alright, since neither of you has done this work, I have. Listen to me and follow my lead. Today is the first day; if we don't finish, we'll be in big trouble."

In truth, Ziyun had never done such work either, but she said this to give them confidence. In this environment, they had to learn to be self-reliant and stick together to survive.

chapters.title: Hardships in the Palace (2)
chapters.content:
Seeing that the carts carrying the manure buckets were parked far from the sewer and the wooden posts used for drying them, Ziyun said to the other two girls, "Let's go and push the carts over to the sewer."

The two girls, knowing nothing else, simply followed her lead.

The three of them pushed a cart to the sewer opening. Ziyun climbed onto the cart and said to them, "I will pass them down to you, and you empty them into the sewer. Remember, you must empty them completely."

The two replied, "Understood!"

Working in coordination, they finished unloading and cleaning the entire cart of manure buckets in no time. Ziyun jumped down and said, "Let's push the carts to the drying area and load up the dried buckets."

Soon, the three of them filled a cart with 20 wooden buckets and parked it to the side.

Because of the scorching sun, the buckets they had just unloaded were already dry by the time they returned, and dry buckets are much harder to scrub clean. Ziyun told the others to move all the buckets to the well and fill them with water to soak.

Wenjuan was so overwhelmed by the stench that she felt like vomiting. Ziyun said to her, "Just imagine that this manure is the Emperor. It is he who caused us to end up like this. If you harbor hatred in your heart, you won't feel so disgusted."

"What if the Emperor finds out?" Wenjuan asked.

"Haha," Ziyun laughed, "If the Emperor found out, he would surely choose you to be his consort, haha."

"Consort?" Xiaocui said, "I’ve become a stinking mess; dreaming of being a consort is just that, a dream."

They had come to the clear realization that their lives were effectively over. Never mind seeing the Emperor; it was uncertain if they would even live for a few more years. The palace was filled with endless dirty and exhausting labor. Even if new people arrived next year to take over the bucket-scrubbing, there would be other tasks waiting. This was fate; one could not help but believe in it.

Although Ziyun had confirmed that she had escaped the clutches of the bully Yang, and Master Wu had sent word that her parents and family had safely fled to another region, she no longer had any worries for her family. She felt fortunate and didn't mind the dirty, tiring work.

Though it was her first time doing such labor, she displayed strong organizational and crisis-management skills that were far beyond the average person. Under her guidance, the three worked in close coordination, and before the sun set, they had finished all their tasks.

Twenty carts were filled with dried buckets and parked to the side, the scrubbed buckets were all hung on the wooden posts, the area around the well was swept clean, and the sewer was covered. The once filthy and foul-smelling courtyard had been transformed.

When it grew dark, Foreman Yan brought the eunuchs to push the carts away. She had assumed the three new girls wouldn't know how to do anything and that the assigned work would certainly not be finished. She had already prepared herself to whip their right buttocks; she couldn't ruin both sides, or they wouldn't be able to lie or sit down, making them unable to work. She didn't mind whipping one side; what she loved most was seeing the bloody welts rise on their fair skin and hearing their screams, which brought her pleasure and satisfaction.

However, when she opened the gate and walked in, she was shocked! These three sixteen-year-old girls had not only finished the work but had also cleaned the courtyard thoroughly. She had no reason to whip them.

"Hmm, not bad." Foreman Yan praised them highly. "You are the most capable girls I have ever seen. I’ve been here for so many years and have never seen anyone as efficient as you. Good, I’ll reward you with an extra dish tonight."

When Foreman Yan was in a normal state of mind, she wasn't entirely unbearable. At dinner, she did indeed give the three girls a bowl of food with a little oil in it.

In the palace, the treatment of palace maids varied. Maids at the very bottom like Ziyun wore coarse cloth, ate grain without oil or meat, and if they fell ill, they received no timely medical treatment, relying entirely on their own constitution to survive. Thus, the mortality rate among low-level maids was high, and few managed to rise above their station. In the palace, the death of a few maids was like the death of a few pets. If a maid died, she was simply wrapped in a quilt and carried out to be buried.

From then on, Foreman Yan could find no fault with the work of the three maids. However, her psychological instability was severe; the less she could find fault, the more she wanted to punish them and find reasons to blame them.

One afternoon, six months later, Foreman Yan came to the girls. "Does no one in your families care about you? Doesn't anyone send you anything?"

Ziyun replied, "My family is too far from the capital; no one can send me anything."

Xiaocui said, "My home is near the palace, right here in Chang'an. But my family doesn't know they can send things. They think that once we enter the palace, we don't have to worry about food or clothing. Now that it's getting cold, we don't even have cotton-padded jackets for winter."

"My home is also very close," Xiaojuan added.

"Tell me your home addresses and your fathers' names. I have a way to pass messages to your families so they can send you cotton jackets and other items," Foreman Yan said, appearing very concerned.

"Thank you, Foreman Yan." Xiaocui and Xiaojuan were grateful, realizing for the first time that their families could send them supplies. They gave her their addresses.

"Wei Ziyun, what about you? Are you just going to freeze to death in winter?" Foreman Yan asked.

"Doesn't the palace issue cotton clothing?" Ziyun asked.

"The girls doing other work get everything, but you don't," Foreman Yan replied coldly. In truth, the palace issued everything to the three girls, but Foreman Yan had intercepted it all.

Ziyun was speechless. She didn't even know where her family had fled to escape the bully Yang. Seeing Ziyun silent, Foreman Yan asked again, "Are you prepared to freeze to death in winter?"

Xiaocui immediately said, "Let my family send an extra set. Ziyun has helped me a lot; I will cover her winter clothes."

Wenjuan also said, "Let my family send an extra set too. Ziyun has helped me a lot as well."

"Fine." Foreman Yan was pleased that Xiaocui and Wenjuan's families could send items. She said with a gentle expression, "You have done your work well and kept the courtyard clean. Don't make any mistakes, or watch out for your buttocks."

Foreman Yan left after saying this.

Ziyun said to Xiaocui and Wenjuan, "Thank you."

Xiaocui said, "What are you thanking me for? Without your help, I wouldn't know how to do anything and would have received many more beatings."

Wenjuan added, "You've helped us so much; it's only right to have a cotton jacket sent for you."

A few days later, the items from their families arrived. Foreman Yan brought three sets of cotton robes, one for each girl. They didn't know what else had been sent, as Foreman Yan had intercepted the rest. Later, they learned that their families had sent silver, clothing, fabric, cosmetics, jewelry, and more, all of which Foreman Yan had claimed for herself.

Having received the goods from Xiaocui and Wenjuan's families, Foreman Yan's attitude toward them improved significantly. However, her attitude toward Ziyun took a 180-degree turn; she found fault with her at every opportunity and frequently whipped her.

Although Ziyun possessed martial arts skills and could have knocked Foreman Yan to the ground with a few moves, she could not do so. In this heavily guarded deep palace, she had to endure. Ziyun often thought: taking a few lashes is still better than marrying the bully Yang. Thus, she not only endured but faced all unjust treatment without a word of complaint.

There were only a few months left before new palace maids would arrive, and they could leave this place and this perverted old woman. She had to be patient.

One day, the three sisters finished their work early. Xiaocui and Wenjuan were sitting in the courtyard basking in the sun, while Ziyun was practicing a martial arts routine with a stick. Foreman Yan usually didn't come until sunset, but today she arrived early. Seeing Ziyun practicing, she began to curse: "You little bitch with no one to look after you, what kind of place do you think this is? Do you know your status? Lift your skirt and raise your buttocks high!"

Ziyun had no choice but to comply. Foreman Yan swung the bamboo board, striking Ziyun's fair, tender buttocks, cursing as she hit: "Little bitch, will you dare to practice again?"

Ziyun cried out in pain: "I won't dare! I won't dare again!"

After ten lashes, half of Ziyun's buttocks were swollen, and the skin was broken in places. But she bit her lip, silently chanting: "Endure, endure, endure!"

After Foreman Yan vented her anger and left, Xiaocui said to Ziyun, "Next time you practice, I'll keep watch at the door so she doesn't see you."

Wenjuan said, "Don't you see? That old woman Yan is bullying Ziyun because her family is far away and can't send gifts. She's looking for trouble on purpose; you can't hide from it."

"Yes," Xiaocui agreed, "I think so too. She wants our silver and goods."

"With the New Year approaching, she hit Ziyun to show us. We should send word to our families to send three New Year gifts. Once she gets the gifts, she won't bother us. Otherwise, we'll be the next ones to get beaten," Wenjuan said, having seen through the old woman.

"Yes," Xiaocui said, "Now that you mention it, I understand. She was giving us a reminder. I had forgotten about the New Year."

"Maybe it's the rules of the palace," Wenjuan said.

"Then let's send word to our families to send three gifts. Once she has them, we can have a peaceful New Year. This is our first New Year in the palace," Xiaocui said.

Ziyun endured the pain and said, "I've caused you both trouble again. If I ever have a chance to rise, I will surely repay you both."

"What are you saying? We thought entering the palace would be a blessing, but who knew we would end up in such misery? We are three sisters sharing life and death. Let's not be polite. You've helped us so much and saved us from so many beatings; we haven't even said thank you. You rest these next few days, and we'll do more of the work," Wenjuan said.

Ziyun could only say, "Thank you!" But she dared not lower her skirt, as the fabric sticking to her wounds was very painful.

At that moment, the eunuch pushing the carts returned. An older eunuch noticed Ziyun had been beaten. He took a small porcelain bottle from his person and said to her, "This is a powder specifically for wounds. Sprinkle it on, and you'll be healed in three days. Hide the bottle well, return it to me tomorrow, and don't let your foreman see it."

"Thank you." Ziyun took the bottle. After the carts were pushed away, she had Xiaocui sprinkle the powder on her wounds and hid the bottle in a crack in the stone. Later, they learned that this eunuch's surname was Gong, and he was a kind-hearted man.

Two days before the New Year, Foreman Yan received the three gifts sent by Xiaocui and Wenjuan's families. She was very pleased and her mood improved. During the New Year, she didn't bother the three maids, and the sisters spent a peaceful holiday.

Yang Guoguang had lost a large sum of silver, failed to get the beauty, and let the Wei family escape; he was filled with rage. During the New Year, he visited a friend in the palace, found out where Wei Ziyun was, and decided to vent all his anger on her.

The most terrifying part was that the Yang family's power and influence were growing, and no one inside or outside the palace dared to oppose them. This time, Yang Guoguang didn't ask his advisor for a plan; he came up with a clever scheme himself: let Ziyun suffer in the palace for a while, and when she couldn't take it anymore, he would find a way to "rescue" her. She would surely be grateful for his great kindness and willingly throw herself into his arms.

This message was passed to Foreman Yan through a eunuch, along with a reward of silver for her services. Foreman Yan accepted the silver and said to the eunuch, "Please tell Master Yang not to worry. I am an expert at this. When this little girl can't take it anymore, I will send word for Master Yang to come and 'rescue' her personally. I guarantee she will be grateful and submissive."

The eunuch said, "As long as you handle this well, you will be a great contributor to Master Yang. Not only will you be rewarded with gold and treasures, but you will also be promoted to a head foreman. You have finally met a benefactor. However, I must remind you: Master Yang wants a pristine beauty. You can make her suffer, but do not damage her skin. A fine piece of leather loses its value if it's damaged, understand?"

"Don't worry, I guarantee that without damaging her skin, I will make her wish she were dead. Please tell Master Yang that I will handle this perfectly."

Foreman Yan hadn't expected such a chance to get rich in her old age. Wei Ziyun, oh Wei Ziyun! I must train you well. But I can't whip her buttocks anymore; if they are ruined, it will be a disaster. Men like a woman's face and her buttocks.

Right, starve her, exhaust her, and see how long she can hold out!

In the palace, eunuchs and maids were managed separately. For example, in the Xingqing Palace where Ziyun was, there was a Chief Eunuch, and for the maids, there was a Head Maid or female official. Foreman Yan was at the lowest level of management. She couldn't keep all the wealth she extorted; she had to pay tribute to her superiors during festivals. Competition among these small foremen and managers was fierce; one slip, and their position would be taken by someone else. Thus, they were extremely eager to please their superiors. After the fifteenth day of the first lunar month, it was the birthday of Foreman Yan's direct superior, and she had to prepare a generous gift.

The source of these gifts was the three maids. Since Ziyun had no gifts to offer, Foreman Yan was furious. Since Master Yang had spoken, it was up to her to break this girl.

Foreman Yan ordered Ziyun to wash 200 manure buckets every day, and she was not allowed to eat until she finished. For a seventeen-year-old girl, washing 200 buckets a day was an immense amount of labor; even with her martial arts skills, it was more than she could bear.

chapters.title: Hardships in the Palace (3)
chapters.content:
When Foreman Yan was not around, Xiaocui and Wenjuan would try to help her scrub a few extra night-soil buckets to lighten her burden.

Despite this, after a full day of work, Ziyun was so exhausted that her waist and legs ached, and she could barely lift her arms. If she made the slightest mistake and Foreman Yan discovered it, she would be punished by being forced to kneel and go without food.

How could a seventeen-year-old girl endure such cruel torment? She already felt that death would be better than life and began to have thoughts of ending it all.

Foreman Yan noticed the change in Ziyun’s mood and immediately realized her opportunity had arrived. She knew that in Ziyun’s eyes, she was the greatest villain, and that anything she said would neither be heard nor believed.

Therefore, she sought out a palace maid named Xiao Yue, who was well-liked and articulate. Although this maid was only twenty-five, she had been in the palace for nearly ten years.

Xiao Yue was considered a big sister to Ziyun; they usually got along well and could talk to each other.

Xiao Yue, of course, understood that if this matter were successful, not only would the reward from Master Yang be substantial, but she would also have a chance for promotion. Thus, she put her heart and soul into the task.

Foreman Yan created the opportunities, and Xiao Yue took advantage of them to approach Ziyun from the side.

Seeing that Ziyun had been punished with kneeling and had not eaten that day, she hid two meat buns and quietly brought them to her.

"Eat them quietly. Don't let anyone see. If Foreman Yan finds out, I’ll be in trouble." Xiao Yue shoved the buns into Ziyun’s hand and left.

Ziyun knew she dared not stay long, so she didn't even dare to say thank you. She swallowed the meat buns in a few gulps; she didn't want to cause trouble for Xiao Yue.

Ziyun was truly starving. It was the first time she had tasted the bitterness of hunger, which was even harder to bear than the dirty, back-breaking labor.

She had swallowed the two meat buns almost whole, neither tasting them nor feeling full.

Xiaocui brought her a ladle of water. "Drink some water."

After Ziyun finished the water, her stomach felt temporarily full.

To torment Ziyun, Foreman Yan would stand at the scene for long periods whenever Ziyun was scrubbing her quota of 200 buckets, so Xiaocui and Wenjuan dared not help even if they wanted to.

They could only rush to scrub the hardest buckets first, leaving the easier ones for Ziyun. When it came to loading and unloading the carts, they also took the lead, trying their best to reduce Ziyun’s heavy labor.

They basically didn't let Ziyun do the work of drying the buckets to lighten her load. However, even so, Ziyun was exhausted every day.

Foreman Yan saw that Ziyun’s physical output was too high. If she didn't have enough food to replenish her energy, she would not only collapse soon but also become emaciated.

The Great Tang Dynasty favored fullness in women as a standard of beauty, the saying went "plump beauties and slender swallows", and a full figure was the only standard for a woman's charm. She couldn't let Ziyun get too thin; she had to keep her well-fed.

The task of getting food to Ziyun was handed to Xiao Yue. This way, it ensured Ziyun wouldn't lose weight while allowing Xiao Yue to curry favor with her.

Ziyun thought she was incredibly lucky to have met Xiao Yue, seeing her as a noble benefactor in her time of crisis and regarding her as the big sister she respected most.

One day, Ziyun returned from being punished, her knees scraped raw. When Xiao Yue saw this, she found some medicine and applied it, saying as she did so, "Your Foreman Yan is too heartless, her hands are so cruel. If you don't leave this place, one day you will die at her hands!"

"Then what can I do? My family is too far away to look after me, no one cares about me. If I don't die here, where else would I die?" Ziyun said helplessly.

"A living person shouldn't be suffocated by their own circumstances. Your benefactor has arrived," Xiao Yue said.

"What benefactor could I possibly have? Sister, don't try to comfort me. Death would be an end to it all; living is just suffering." Ziyun truly had thoughts of death.

"Little sister, you are still so young, don't have thoughts of ending your life. As the saying goes, it's better to live a miserable life than to die a good death. I heard Master Yang has taken a fancy to you. Isn't this your good fortune?" Xiao Yue said, referring to the bully, Master Yang.

"That old, undying thing! I would rather die than see him!" Ziyun said firmly.

"Silly girl," Xiao Yue persuaded, "Master Yang is already over fifty. How much longer can he live? If you agree to him, he will take you out immediately. You know the power of the Yang family. Once you arrive at his home, you will surely be the most favored, enjoying endless wealth and glory!"

Ziyun shook her head and said indignantly, "I am his sworn enemy; I will never submit to him!"

"My silly sister, you are only in your teens, and he is over fifty. Can he outlive you?" Xiao Yue asked.

"He certainly can't outlive me."

"Once he passes, won't you inherit a portion of the property? With that wealth, you won't have to worry about food or drink for the rest of your life. How old will you be then? At most, you'll be my age. You can then find a husband to your liking and live a happy life. Wouldn't that be great?" Xiao Yue urged.

"If you think it's so good, why don't you go?" Ziyun asked.

"Oh my, I don't have that kind of luck. Master Yang has his eyes on you. If he had his eyes on me, I would have gone long ago!"

Xiao Yue truly didn't have that luck. She had no connections at home, nor did she have the silver to bribe the superiors, so she had been struggling at the very bottom for ten years, never even managing to get a supervisory position.

"Sister Xiao Yue, I know you mean well. But it's impossible! I won't see that old thing even if I die. Sister Xiao Yue, please tell that Master Yang to give up on this idea!"

Ziyun’s tone allowed for no negotiation.

"My silly sister, you wash night-soil buckets every day, has your brain been filled with filth? Why are you unwilling to accept such a good thing?" Xiao Yue truly didn't understand why Ziyun was unwilling to marry Master Yang.

"Sister Xiao Yue, if I asked you to eat night-soil for three days in exchange for wealth and glory, would you do it?" Ziyun asked.

"Haha," Xiao Yue laughed, "Is Master Yang really that disgusting?"

"You'll know when you see him. Being with him is even more disgusting than eating night-soil!" Ziyun said, making a look of extreme disgust.

"Haha!" Xiao Yue laughed loudly, "If Master Yang knew you hated him so much, he would surely go mad with anger. Alright, think about it carefully. No need to rush. When you've made up your mind, give me a definite answer. I'll come to see you when I have the chance."

Xiao Yue knew that one couldn't eat hot tofu in a hurry; it had to be done slowly. So, she didn't force Ziyun to commit.

Having said this much, although Ziyun was young, she understood Xiao Yue’s words. She realized then that Xiao Yue was a lobbyist for the bully, Master Yang.

And Foreman Yan was cooperating with them to break her. She finally understood why her work had become increasingly bitter and painful, the true culprit was the bully, Master Yang. What to do? The more she thought about it, the more terrifying it felt.

Her movements in the palace were already in the hands of the bully, and she couldn't escape his clutches. What should she do? She asked herself repeatedly.

In the end, she resolved to grit her teeth and endure. She had no other way but to endure.

Wenjuan was a bit more cunning. After Xiao Yue left, she whispered to Ziyun, "I see it now. Foreman Yan and Xiao Yue are playing the 'good cop, bad cop' routine. They are both Master Yang's people."

Reminded by Wenjuan, Ziyun seemed to understand one thing: with the bully "looking after" her, the people in the palace wouldn't dare do anything too extreme to her.

At most, they would make her suffer more hardship and labor to force her to submit. Even Foreman Yan wouldn't dare to kill her, as they had to ensure they handed over an intact beauty to the bully.

Ziyun finally realized that a path to survival lay right at her feet. So she said to Wenjuan, "Don't worry about me, I'll be fine. I have a way to deal with them."

Xiao Yue reported Ziyun’s stance to the eunuch she was in contact with, though she didn't close the door entirely, leaving Master Yang feeling there was still hope.

If Master Yang felt there was no hope and gave up, she wouldn't get any benefits. When the bully received this news, he was not angry but happy.

He told his subordinates, "A horse that isn't spirited isn't a good horse, and a woman without a temper isn't a fun woman. I just like women with strong spirits; it's interesting to tame such a woman. You don't need to be anxious. Grind her down slowly; I must make her submit to me wholeheartedly."

"Master is brilliant!" his subordinates praised.

"Don't worry, before long, she will kneel and beg me, and finally become the little darling in my bed. Do you believe me?" The bully was very confident in himself.

"We believe! We have no doubt!"

The bully’s subordinates conveyed his meaning to the palace and gave reward money to both Xiao Yue and Foreman Yan.

When Xiao Yue and Foreman Yan met, they laughed until they were doubled over.

"With one of us playing the good cop and the other the bad cop, I don't believe this stubborn girl won't soften up! Just watch, when Master Yang rewards us again, I will definitely recommend you for a promotion." Foreman Yan was already beside herself with joy.

"With your methods, even if she doesn't soften up, she'll lose a layer of skin! Has she ever eaten braised pork and rice since she came in?" Xiao Yue asked.

"Heh heh, I haven't even eaten it, where would she get any?" Foreman Yan said.

"That's good. Tomorrow I'll get a bowl of braised pork and rice. She needs to taste something good; don't let her forget the taste of delicious food. Only by having both bitterness and sweetness can there be a contrast, and only with contrast will she have desire. We can't always let her suffer; we must let her see hope. I believe it won't be long before she begs me for good food. Won't our great task be accomplished then?" Xiao Yue said with great confidence.

However, the next day, Ziyun’s performance shocked Foreman Yan! Ziyun acted completely out of character; she refused to do any of the work that was supposed to be hers.

She was seen dressed neatly, sitting in the chair Foreman Yan usually occupied, watching Xiaocui and Wenjuan work.

Seeing this, Foreman Yan was filled with rage. She raised the bamboo board in her hand and struck toward Ziyun.

Ziyun remained calm, raised her hand to block Foreman Yan’s arm, and with a flick of her wrist, snatched the bamboo board away. She snapped it in two with a light motion, which gave Foreman Yan a huge fright. She hadn't expected this little girl, Wei Ziyun, to have such great strength!

Her movements were as agile as a man's. Ziyun threw the bamboo board to the ground and said to Foreman Yan, "Be more polite to me from now on, or be careful, or I might just turn on you."

After saying this, to show off her martial arts, she kicked a dried-out night-soil bucket into the air, and as it fell, she reached out a hand and caught it lightly.

This action scared Xiaocui and Wenjuan silly, and Foreman Yan fled in a panic.

Wenjuan exclaimed, "Ziyun, are you human or a god?"

Ziyun replied, "I am human, of course."

"Your martial arts are truly amazing!" Xiaocui praised.

"I practiced when I was a child," Ziyun said.

"No wonder you don't look tired even when doing heavy labor. Your martial arts are so powerful! Now it's great, Foreman Yan won't dare to bully you again. Look at how scared she was!"

Before Xiaocui’s voice had even faded, Foreman Yan returned with several burly women. Some held wooden sticks, others held ropes, and they surrounded Ziyun aggressively.

This formation scared Xiaocui and Wenjuan into hiding in a corner, not daring to get close.

Foreman Yan said to the women, "Tie this little bitch up for me first. Don't hit her face, but hit everywhere else as hard as you can!"

The women saw it was just a young girl and didn't take her seriously; any one of them could beat this little girl to a pulp.
