He thought, This girl is truly capable. Even I am a bit afraid of these women, yet she has them wrapped around her finger.

"Wei Ziyun, come here." Eunuch Gong called her aside.

"Greetings, Eunuch Gong."

"Never mind that. You must answer my questions honestly, understand?"

"I understand. Please ask, and I will answer truthfully." Ziyun already realized the matter of the poem had reached the imperial court. Whether it was a blessing or a curse, she didn't know, but she suspected it was more likely a curse. Death is death, she thought, no point in hiding.

"Did you sew that extra-large cotton battle robe?"

"Reporting to you, it was indeed sewn by this servant."

"Did you write that poem?"

"Reporting to you, it was indeed written by this servant."

"Can you guarantee that you did both of these things?"

"Reporting to you, I can guarantee it!"

"Good! In a moment, I will take you to see Lord Gao. Answer whatever he asks truthfully, without the slightest concealment, understand?"

"Reporting to you, I understand. Thank you, Eunuch."

"Let me give you a hint: the Emperor has already granted you amnesty. So, don't be afraid, and absolutely do not lie. Whatever Lord Gao asks, answer truthfully. Your good fortune has arrived!"

"Thank you, Eunuch. I will keep it in mind. If one day I rise in the world, I will surely repay your great kindness!"

"I have worked in the imperial court all my life, and you are the first extraordinary woman I have ever seen. I believe you will have a bright future. Come with me. Be polite when you see Lord Gao; do not be afraid or panicked. You are now a person of the Emperor and the Consort; no one will dare to do anything to you. Remember that?"

"Reporting to you, I have kept it in my heart."

A short while later, Eunuch Gong brought Ziyun before Gao Lishi.

"This servant Wei Ziyun pays respects to Lord Gao."

"Get up, no need for formalities." Gao Lishi saw only an ordinary little palace maid; she didn't have three heads or six arms.

"You are Wei Ziyun?"

"Reporting to you, my Lord, I am indeed Wei Ziyun."

"Raise your head and speak."

"As you command, my Lord." Ziyun raised her head.

Gao Lishi looked at her. She had the appearance of a beautiful young girl, with nothing to suggest she knew martial arts. He first had to verify if she wrote the poem to answer to the Emperor.

He asked, "Did you make an extra-large cotton battle robe?"

"Reporting to you, yes. I used the leftover fabric and cotton from making the robes because it would have been a waste not to, and I made an extra-large one so that those tall and mighty warriors could wear it."

"There was a poem inside that robe. Did you write it?"

"Reporting to you, I wrote it."

"It really was you? The Emperor has already granted you amnesty. If it wasn't you, you would be guilty of deceiving the Emperor. Do you know the consequences?"

"Reporting to you, I know. The crime of deceiving the Emperor is punishable by beheading."

"Very good, you know everything. I ask you, where did you hide the poem in the battle robe?" Gao Lishi tested her.

"Reporting to you, I sewed the poem into the collar of the battle robe."

"Hmm. Can you recite the poem you wrote?"

Ziyun had answered the first question correctly. As for the second, if she hadn't written it, there would be no way for her to answer.

Ziyun recited the poem, and it matched the poem submitted by General Guo word for word, proving that she was indeed the author.

Gao Lishi verified Wei Ziyun’s identity, and the stone in his heart finally fell. He had found the author and could now answer to the Emperor.

"May I ask, Lord Gao, has the Emperor truly granted me amnesty?" Ziyun thought, Since I'm going to die anyway, I might as well ask to be sure. So she dared to ask Gao Lishi.

"There are no jokes in the palace. Your good fortune has arrived! Go, wash your face, comb your hair, find some festive clothes to wear, and come with me to see the Emperor."

"I obey the command!"

Hearing that Gao Lishi was taking Ziyun to see the Emperor, the other maids were stunned! They rushed to help Ziyun fetch water, find rouge, lipstick, and powder.

Usually, Ziyun didn't wear makeup. She dressed simply because she spent her days around night-soil buckets; even if she had nice clothes, she couldn't wear them.

Wenjuan found a new skirt and asked Gao Lishi, "Lord Gao, how is this skirt?"

Gao Lishi looked at it carefully and said, "It will do. After she washes her face and puts on her makeup, let me see her."

The maids quickly tidied Ziyun up. She put on the new skirt, and Gao Lishi nodded. "Alright, come with me."

"Lord Gao, I dare to ask, will Ziyun be able to come back after she goes?" Xiaocui asked, and everyone froze.

Some thought: Is the Emperor going to behead Ziyun? Private communication with the outside world is a major taboo!

Others thought: I heard they give prisoners good food and drink before beheading them. Lord Gao is being so nice, could it be...

No one dared to guess anything good, because these people had never heard of a good thing happening to a lowly palace maid.

chapters.title: Blessings Cultivated Over Ten Thousand Lifetimes
chapters.content:
As Ziyun followed Gao Lishi out of Xingqing Palace, she kept thinking to herself, "Is all of this real? Could it be a trap? Oh, whatever. The worst that can happen is death. I’m not even afraid of dying, so what else is there to fear?" With this thought, she cast aside her mental burdens and distractions, following Gao Lishi to meet the Emperor.

As they neared the Changsheng Hall, Gao Lishi stopped and said to Ziyun, "Little girl, do not be afraid. This is a blessing you cultivated in your past life. Meeting the merciful Emperor of this dynasty is your great fortune in this life. Do you know the proper etiquette for meeting the Emperor?"

"In reply to your words, my lord," Ziyun said, "how would a humble girl like me know the rules for meeting the Emperor? I humbly ask for your guidance, Lord Gao."

Ziyun had heard of court etiquette when she first entered the palace and knew a little, but she wanted to hear more from Eunuch Gao regarding the specific protocols for an imperial audience.

Gao Lishi knew that a low-ranking palace maid who had been in the palace for only a year could not possibly know the intricate rules of the court. He proceeded to explain the necessary precautions for the audience.

Then he asked, "Do you understand?"

"In reply to your words, my lord," Ziyun answered, "the humble girl understands. Thank you for your guidance."

"Good," Gao Lishi instructed. "Do not panic when you see the Emperor and the Consort. Just follow the etiquette I taught you. Answer only what they ask you, and do not be loose-lipped or create unnecessary complications. Do you remember?"

"In reply to your words, my lord, the humble girl has taken it to heart." Ziyun knew exactly what should and should not be said.

During the three days Gao Lishi spent carrying out the imperial order to find the maid who wrote the poem, the Emperor and Consort Yang had been discussing this sentimental, clever, and daring young maid.

"Your Majesty, I have been wondering, could the soldier who received the padded battle robe be a wounded veteran?" The Consort was worried that the maid might be marrying a disabled man.

"My beloved, you worry too much. There have been no major conflicts on the border in recent years. Without a war, how could there be wounded soldiers?" Although the Emperor lived deep within the palace, he was well-informed about the situation at the frontiers.

"Your Majesty, did General Guo mention what the soldier who received the poem is like?" The Consort was also very concerned about the soldier.

"Guess," the Emperor teased.

"I am dull-witted; how could I possibly guess?" the Consort replied, acting coyly before the Emperor.

"This little maid is quite clever. She made the padded robe extra large and loose. What kind of person could wear that?" The Emperor, always sharper than others, gave the Consort a hint.

"I understand now! Only a tall and powerful soldier could wear such a robe! This little girl is so clever, hehe." The Consort was not dull at all; she caught on immediately and beamed with joy.

The Emperor was naturally pleased and said to her, "Do you women all like tall and powerful men?" The Emperor had his own streak of jealousy.

The Emperor himself was a tall and powerful man. Historians described him as: "Naturally wise and decisive, proficient in music, and possessing a majestic and handsome appearance."

"Your Majesty, I only like you!" the Consort said, leaning against his side. She had become adept at handling such questions.

Hearing this, the Emperor felt as comforted as if he were being stroked by a pair of soft hands. He said to her, "According to General Guo’s report, the soldier who received the poem is not only tall and powerful but also young and brave. The General spoke highly of him. It is just that he is a low-ranking soldier; he wouldn't be able to support our girl if he married her."

"Then what shall we do?" The Consort knew the Emperor had a solution, but she deliberately refrained from asking or suggesting anything. It was best to let the Emperor propose the good deed himself so he would be happy. If she said everything, what sense of superiority would the Emperor have?

"Haha, my beloved, do not worry. I have already issued an imperial decree to promote the lad three ranks. A girl of the imperial household must at least marry an officer."

"On behalf of Ziyun and that lad, I thank Your Majesty. I knew you would arrange everything for them. Long live the Emperor, may you live for ten thousand years!"

"Are these matters even considered 'matters' to me?"

"In reply to Your Majesty, these things are indeed trifles to you. But for them, these are earth-shattering events! Your Majesty’s fulfillment of their wishes is like a heavenly blessing. That soldier will surely be loyal to the country, fight bravely, and become a faithful guardian of the court!"

"My beloved, your words are very insightful. Bring the wine!" The Emperor ordered the eunuchs to set up a banquet.

When the Emperor was happy, he wanted food, drink, and music. The banquet began, the musicians played, and the melody of the "Rainbow Skirt and Feather Dress" dance filled the air. The Consort not only loved this piece but took pride and joy in performing it.

Legend had it that the Emperor had dreamed he entered the Moon Palace, heard celestial music, and saw hundreds of maidens in white silk dancing. He memorized the melody, brought it back to the mortal world, and incorporated the Indian "Brahman Melody" into it. Later, the Consort created the dance, naming it the "Rainbow Skirt and Feather Dress."

The Emperor loved this piece most of all; he never tired of hearing it. The Consort was obsessed with it; she never tired of dancing it.

When the music ended, the Emperor was tipsy, and the Consort was drenched in sweat from her spirited performance. The Emperor loved the scent of her sweat above all else.

Usually, the Consort did not sweat, except when she danced with great passion. Her sweat was like a human perfume, possessing a deep, enchanting fragrance that no artificial blend could replicate.

When the Consort’s fragrance filled the air, the Emperor was at his happiest and most satisfied. At such moments, any favor requested would be granted.

The Consort, knowing this, knelt before the Emperor while he was in high spirits and said, "Your Majesty, I would like to request a favor for this palace maid."

"I knew you would say that. Get up and tell me, what favor do you want?"

"I wish to provide this maid with more dowry, specifically cloth and cotton. I hear the border is very cold in winter, and she has nothing."

"Granted!" For the Emperor, providing a dowry for a girl leaving the palace was a trivial matter.

"Thank you, Your Majesty! Long live the Emperor!"

Just as they were speaking, Gao Lishi arrived with Ziyun.

"By imperial decree, I, Gao Lishi, bring the palace maid Wei Ziyun to see the Emperor!"

"Bring her in!"

Gao Lishi and Ziyun knelt before the Emperor and the Consort, shouting, "Long live the Emperor! May the Consort live for a thousand years!"

"Rise, Lord Gao."

Gao Lishi stood respectfully to the side.

The Emperor asked Ziyun, "Your name is Wei Ziyun?"

"In reply to Your Majesty," Ziyun said, not daring to look up, "this humble servant is indeed Wei Ziyun."

"Look up when you speak."

Ziyun looked up. Seeing her upright features and fair skin, the Emperor and Consort were reassured; she would not bring shame to the imperial household.

"I ask you, why did you make such an oversized padded battle robe?"

"In reply to Your Majesty," Ziyun answered, "I admire the tall, powerful heroes and warriors who fight for our country."

"What was your purpose in writing the poem?"

"In reply to Your Majesty, my purpose was twofold: first, to promote imperial grace; second, to boost the morale of the troops."

Ziyun’s words stunned everyone present. Even the Emperor had not expected such impassioned words from a little maid.

The Emperor looked at her seriously, thinking: I must challenge her to see how she handles it.

With that, he said, "I have issued a decree pardoning you and fulfilling your fated connection with the soldier who received the poem. However, I must tell you the current state of this soldier."

The Emperor paused, watching her. The Consort and Gao Lishi waited for him to continue.

Ziyun finally confirmed that the Emperor had truly pardoned her and sanctioned the marriage. She waited, thinking that no matter what the Emperor demanded or what he said about the soldier, she would agree to everything.

The Emperor continued, "According to reports, the soldier who received your poem is indeed tall and powerful and brave in battle. However, in a fight against the Turks, he was severely wounded. He lost an ear, a leg, and an arm. He is only half a man now. Are you still willing to marry him? If not, I will find you another husband."

"In reply to Your Majesty, his injuries were sustained for you and for the nation! He is a hero of the Great Tang! No matter how severely disabled he is, I admire him, and I am willing to marry him and serve him for the rest of my life!"

Ziyun’s answer was decisive, crisp, and firm.

"Hmm." The Emperor nodded deeply. Ziyun had not only passed his test, but her sincere and impassioned response left him very satisfied.

Gao Lishi was delighted. He hadn't taught her those words; he truly had to look at this little maid with new eyes.

"Are you truly willing to serve a disabled soldier for life, without regret?" the Emperor asked further.

"In reply to Your Majesty, I will serve him for life, without regret!" Ziyun thought to herself that this was still much better than serving the bully Yang.

The Emperor decided to give the Consort some face. He said to Ziyun, "Before you came in, the Consort requested a favor for you. She worries you will have nothing at the border, so she has provided a dowry of five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred loads of cotton. The Consort has even more for you."

Gao Lishi immediately pulled Ziyun to kowtow, "Thank you for your grace, Your Majesty! Long live the Emperor! May the Consort live for a thousand years!"

The Emperor looked at the Consort, who nodded.

The Emperor told Gao Lishi, "Take Ziyun to collect her dowry."

Gao Lishi again pulled Ziyun to kowtow, "Thank you for your grace, Your Majesty! Long live the Emperor! May the Consort live for a thousand years!"

"Rise, go. Pack your things and depart early." The Emperor turned to the musicians and said, "Play!"

A head maid led Gao Lishi and Ziyun to the Consort’s palace to collect the dowry.

The next day, Gao Lishi and the eunuchs escorted Ziyun out of the palace. The imperial dowry filled several carts. Gao Lishi handed Ziyun over to General Guo Ziyi and asked him to preside over their wedding.

General Guo thanked the two eunuchs and set off with Ziyun.

Not long after leaving Chang'an, General Guo asked, "Girl, the Emperor gave you quite a dowry. It fills so many carts. What is in them?"

"In reply to the General," Ziyun said, "five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred loads of cotton. Plus the valuables and gold and silver jewelry from the Consort."

"This is truly the first time such a thing has happened. How did you think of hiding a poem in a padded battle robe?"

"In reply to the General," Ziyun said, "it was a move of desperation." She then recounted how the bully Yang had framed her father and how she had been forced to become a palace maid.

"So that’s how it was!" Although General Guo was at odds with Yang Guozhong, he could do nothing about him. He felt sympathy for this wise and courageous maid.

General Guo personally delivered Ziyun to Muci Mountain and presided over the wedding of Chen Huiguang and Wei Ziyun.

This was an unprecedented and unique event in the Muci Mountain region.

At the wedding, General Guo announced Chen Huiguang’s promotion.

The news caused an uproar in the camp!

"Skinny Monkey" summarized Chen Huiguang’s two "firsts": he was the first poor lad to marry a palace maid, and he was the first to be promoted three ranks in peacetime, rising from a soldier to an officer.

Everyone said that Chen Huiguang had hit the jackpot; marrying a wife and getting a promotion, such great fortune had fallen upon him for no reason.

The soldiers and civilians of Muci Mountain had endless discussions about this "fallen from heaven" palace maid, eventually turning her into a legendary figure.

But one decision by Ziyun made everyone, including Chen Huiguang, look at her with newfound respect.

When Ziyun saw that some soldiers and their families still lacked warm clothing, she immediately decided to donate all five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred loads of cotton to the soldiers and civilians of Muci Mountain.

This was a lifesaver, solving their winter clothing crisis, truly a gift of charcoal in the snow.

Neither General Guo Ziyi nor the Muci Mountain commander, Zhao Shan, had expected such generosity from a little maid.

Even with all their power, the two generals could not have procured five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred loads of cotton.

They not only liked the little maid but were forced to hold her in high regard, sensing that she would become a legend in Muci Mountain.

Chen Huiguang became famous locally. Skinny Monkey told him the rumors: "At first, no one believed you married a beautiful palace maid. Then, seeing the dowry and General Guo presiding over the wedding, everyone believed it. They say your fate was destined. An old fortune teller said your marriage was decided in a past life."

"I think so too. Look, my family is so poor, and I’m just a common soldier. I never dared to dream of marrying; I was just happy to have a meal." Chen Huiguang hadn't married yet simply because he was too poor.

"Exactly," Skinny Monkey agreed. "Look at you: you have the height, the looks, the education, and the martial arts; you win every competition in the camp. But you couldn't get promoted, and without a promotion, how could you marry?"

"Nonsense. As a common soldier, if I married, I’d just be making a woman suffer!" In any dynasty, the treatment of a common soldier was the lowest.

Because Chen Huiguang had married a wife with such a special status, his superiors dared not neglect him. They rushed to arrange housing, furniture, and kitchenware for him.

Thus, he didn't spend a single copper on his wedding, nor did he have to worry; everything was arranged for him by those above.

chapters.title: This Palace Maid Is No Simple Character
chapters.content:
Although Miss Ziyun was the daughter of a county magistrate, marrying a common soldier was not exactly a satisfying prospect for her. However, she had escaped the clutches of the bully Yang and freed herself from the devil’s entanglement, which was something to be thankful for.

Although Chen Huiguang’s family background was poor, his character, physique, and appearance were all excellent. She felt she had struck gold, ending up with a tall, powerful, and nearly perfect hunk like Chen Huiguang, rather than the wounded or disabled man the Emperor had described.

Before meeting Chen Huiguang, Miss Ziyun had prepared herself mentally. She could not treat the Emperor’s words as a joke, nor did she dare to. She had assumed Chen Huiguang was a disabled man, and she had already promised the Emperor that she would follow and serve this disabled man for the rest of her life.

Therefore, when she met Chen Huiguang and saw a handsome man with a square face, large ears, elegant eyes, dragon-like brows, and a majestic stature, she was truly overjoyed, beyond happy! Only then did she realize the Emperor’s good intentions, and she decided to start a new life with him.

After settling down, Miss Ziyun began to inquire about her parents and family. However, they had left Chang'an quietly, and no one knew their whereabouts. How could it be easy to find them?

Miss Ziyun had come to the desolate and cold Muci Mountain all by herself. She had no relatives there; apart from her husband, she didn't even have anyone to talk to.

General Guo had escorted her to Muci Mountain, a journey that took half a month, during which she had built trust and friendship with him. However, General Guo left Muci Mountain immediately after hosting their wedding, and she regretted not entrusting him to help inquire about her parents' whereabouts.

She didn't know anyone in Muci Mountain. The Yang family’s influence was vast; who knew if the people here had any connections to them? Thus, she dared not trust anyone.

The news that Miss Ziyun had been betrothed by the Emperor to a soldier at the border spread quickly, and the bully Yang soon heard of it. However, no matter how powerful the Yang family was, they dared not defy the Emperor, and all for the sake of a concubine! So, the bully Yang gave up on the idea and stopped searching for or seeking revenge against the Wei family.

At this time, Yang Guozhong was busy with major construction projects, building a massive complex of palaces. He connected the residences belonging to the Yang family, the Prime Minister’s mansion, the Prince Consort’s mansion, the Korea Mansion, the Qin Mansion, and others, into one continuous expanse. The pavilions were grand and towering, the corridors faced each other, and the main roads were so wide and straight that ten horses could gallop side by side.

During the Kaiyuan era’s golden age, the power and luxury of the Yang family had reached its peak. The people of the Yang family, including those associated with them, were incredibly arrogant. It was a universally acknowledged fact that the Emperor was number one, and the Yang family was number two.

Even the veteran official Li Linfu had to bow to Yang Guozhong and yield to him.

Therefore, it was truly incredible that Miss Ziyun had managed to escape the Yang family’s clutches. Since she had not only turned the incredible into reality but also successfully and respectably married out of the palace, those who couldn't fathom it could only explain it by saying she was protected by divine beings.

Many more said it was the good fortune she had cultivated in her past life that had come to help her through the tribulations of this one.

General Zhao Shan, the commander of Muci Mountain, also had many doubts about this matter. He asked Deputy Commander Li Hu, "Tell me, our Muci Mountain only has one tall and powerful soldier, Chen Huiguang. How did this palace maid happen to pick him?"

"Haha, the Commander hasn't managed military supplies, so you don't know the mystery behind this."

"What? There’s a mystery?" Commander Zhao asked, somewhat surprised. "Even if she’s a clever palace maid, the palace is thousands of miles away. How could she know about our situation here? How did she manage to pick the only tall and powerful warrior? Why didn't she pick a scrawny one?"

"Hehe, listen to me explain," Deputy Commander Li, wanting to show off his intelligence before the Commander, said eloquently: "This little palace maid probably didn't expect the Emperor to show such extraordinary grace and fulfill her marriage wishes. I reckon she only wanted to find a man she liked for her next life."

"Hmm, that’s interesting. Go on." The Commander began to see the point.

"Women, no matter how tall they are, all like tall and powerful men. How could she find one?"

"Oh, I see," the Commander realized, "by making an oversized cotton battle robe that only a tall and powerful man could wear! Haha! This little palace maid is very calculating; she cannot be underestimated!"

"Commander, she donated all five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred piculs of cotton that the Emperor gave as a dowry to our soldiers and their families. What is your take on this?"

"This is exactly the important matter I wanted to discuss with you. If you were given five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred piculs of cotton, would you donate them all?"

"Oh, this... this... I wouldn't donate them all. I’d have to keep some for myself, right? What about you, sir?" The Deputy Commander couldn't quite wrap his head around Ziyun’s act of donating everything.

"Haha, I wouldn't donate it all either; I’d keep some for myself. It seems we are just ordinary people and cannot compare to this little palace maid. She is no ordinary person!"

"Furthermore, this Chen Huiguang was promoted three ranks for no reason. The soldiers are not convinced!"

"You don't need to worry about that. His promotion has nothing to do with you or me; it is the Emperor’s decree. Who isn't convinced? Does anyone dare to defy the imperial order?" Commander Zhao felt the same way as everyone else, but it was an imperial decree, who would dare to defy it?

In truth, no one was convinced by Chen Huiguang’s triple promotion; it was obvious. Everyone dared to be angry but not speak out, only grumbling in private.

"We’ll just have to accept it," the Deputy Commander said helplessly.

"There is a big matter, I wonder if you’ve thought of it?" Commander Zhao asked.

"What big matter? Please enlighten me, Commander."

"Tell me, would the Emperor send a palace maid to our border for no reason? Is this a trap? Is there some other underlying cause?"

"With your guidance, Commander, although I am dull, I also sense that this little palace maid is not simple. I have served in the Great Tang for almost a lifetime, and this is the first time I’ve seen a palace maid get married and sent to the border. You are experienced and knowledgeable, have you ever seen a second case?"

"I have never heard of such a thing either. Otherwise, why would I suspect that this matter is not so simple? It seems Muci Mountain will no longer be as peaceful as it used to be!"

"Then, what should we do? Please instruct me, Commander."

"Do nothing. Wait and see how things develop!"

"I obey!"

Because the marriage was so sudden, the wedding was held the very day General Guo arrived at Muci Mountain with Miss Ziyun.

The next day, General Guo left Muci Mountain due to his busy official duties.

Chen Huiguang didn't have time to bring his parents to the wedding, and Miss Ziyun had no way to bring hers. Thus, neither side had parents present.

Chen Huiguang and Ziyun’s "honeymoon" passed in a flash. Chen Huiguang returned to the main camp to take up his duties and couldn't stay home to accompany his new bride. Ziyun was left alone at home, and naturally, she felt very bored and lonely.

The young women and wives in the military family quarters were full of curiosity about this palace maid who had descended from the sky. After receiving the cloth and cotton Ziyun had donated, they were also filled with gratitude.

Seeing her home alone, the bolder young wives brought their needlework to keep her company and chat. At first, only one or two dared to go to Ziyun’s house, but within a few days, her home became a gathering place for the wives.

Whenever Chen Huiguang was away, they would come to Ziyun’s house to do their needlework. Over time, these wives became good friends with Ziyun, talking about everything.

They talked about the Zhangs and the Lis, mothers-in-law, sisters-in-law, who was fighting, who was arguing; they talked about everything, laughing and having a wonderful time all day long.

Once they were all very familiar, a wife named Xiaohong asked Ziyun, "The Emperor wouldn't have only given you that cloth and cotton as a dowry, would he?" They wanted to see the gold, silver, jewelry, and silk the Emperor must have given her.

"To tell you the truth, the dowry the Emperor bestowed upon me was only that cloth and cotton; there were no valuables."

"Oh, we don't want your things, we’re just curious and want to see. Be generous and show us so we can feast our eyes!" Xiaohong’s words represented everyone’s wishes.

"Exactly, the Emperor couldn't have failed to bestow gold and silver jewelry upon you. Take them out and let us see; it won't hurt them," a young wife named Shuangshuang echoed.

Although the others didn't speak, they looked at Ziyun with eager eyes. Seeing this, Ziyun had to come clean: "The dowry the Emperor gave me really was only that. However, the Noble Consort also bestowed some dowry upon me. Would you like to see that?"

"Dowry from the Noble Consort? We want to see! We really want to see!" the wives shouted.

Ziyun opened a large wooden chest she had brought from the palace and took out a small bundle. She placed it on the table and opened it, revealing a pair of jade bracelets, a gold hairpin, a pair of gold earrings, a pearl necklace, and a jade rouge box.

Ziyun pointed to the jewelry and said to the wives, "These are the ornaments the Noble Consort bestowed upon me."

"Wow!" The wives gasped in amazement. They had never seen such exquisite jewelry. Every piece was crafted with great care; they were all masterpieces.

Seeing their interest, Ziyun took out some dresses from the chest: "These are several skirts made of silk, this is a misty green smoke shirt with scattered flowers, these are several rainbow dresses, and this is a feather garment..."

When the feather garment was taken out, everyone stared with wide eyes, not daring to breathe. Ziyun asked, "Is it beautiful?"

Xiaohong said, "It’s too beautiful!"

"You should put it away quickly; it’s too precious, don't let us break it." Shuangshuang wanted to touch it but was afraid of damaging it, so she pulled back her hand.

Ziyun said nonchalantly, "It’s fine, go ahead and touch it."

Shuangshuang said, "You should put it away. Things from the Noble Consort are rare treasures; you must keep them safe."

Everyone else agreed, "Put it away quickly."

Ziyun had no choice but to put the valuables away.

As the saying goes, "To make friends, you must give your heart; friends who don't give their hearts don't last." Ziyun had shown them the dowry bestowed by the Emperor and the Noble Consort without reservation, which was a sign of opening her heart.

Seeing Ziyun’s sincerity and honesty, these wives treated her as a good friend. Over time, they became close confidantes who talked about everything.

Moreover, Ziyun was a young lady of a prominent family who had seen the world, had her own opinions, and was capable. They couldn't help but treat her as their leader. Whenever something happened at home, they told her, and if they had any unpleasantness, they sought her advice.

Ziyun not only enjoyed listening to their chatter but also helped them come up with ideas and solutions, resolving many family conflicts for them. Over time, Ziyun became their backbone and the person they were most willing to confide in, even their pillar of support.

In times of peace, the border was not entirely secure. An incident that occurred in the military family quarters not only reminded the soldiers that war could happen at any time but also made all the soldiers and their families look at Ziyun with newfound respect.

The incident went like this: One day, two strange men appeared in the family quarters. From their appearance, they looked like local herdsmen. However, local herdsmen never wandered into the military family quarters.

A meddlesome young wife named Wei Ping felt something was wrong with these two men and found Ziyun. She said, "Huiguang’s wife, two strangers have come into our courtyard. They don't look like locals; the local herdsmen never come here. Could they be Turkic spies?"

Wei Ping was the wife of Centurion Li Deshun. She was the "know-it-all" of the courtyard, knew everyone’s family, and loved to meddle in everyone’s business.

"It’s too late to notify our troops immediately. Here’s what we’ll do: go find a few strong wives, take sticks and ropes, and wait at my house. I’ll go take a look and come right back." Ziyun took a long stick and went out.

Ziyun followed the two men from a distance. From behind, they looked no different from local herdsmen, and one of them had a large sack slung over his shoulder. However, their behavior of looking around suspiciously caught Ziyun’s attention.

If locals came to the family quarters to do business or find someone, they would head toward a specific house or ask for directions. These two were wandering aimlessly, and Ziyun knew what was up.

When she returned home, six or seven brave wives were already waiting for her with sticks and ropes, including Shuangshuang and Xiaohong.

"Don't be afraid, follow behind me. They have walked into a dead end and will turn back soon. I will go and question them first. Don't act yet, in case they are our own people."

"Okay, we’ll listen to you," Shuangshuang said.

When the two men reached the dead end and turned back, passing by Ziyun’s door, Ziyun suddenly pushed the door open and shouted at them, "Who are you looking for?"

The two men hadn't seen anyone outside after entering the quarters. Startled by Ziyun’s sudden shout, they looked and saw only a weak woman with no one else around, so they revealed their sinister faces.

Both men pulled out waist knives from their robes. The one with the sack dropped it and lunged viciously at Ziyun! The other stood guard.

The wives standing at Ziyun’s door were terrified at the sight of the knives. Although they had sticks and ropes, they were very afraid, as none of them had ever faced a Turk in battle.

Xiaohong shouted to Ziyun, "Huiguang’s wife, be careful!"

But Ziyun met the attacker with her stick. Before the wives could even see what happened, the man rushing at Ziyun was knocked to the ground.

Ziyun shouted to the wives, "Tie him up tight!"

The wives swarmed forward and, in a flurry of activity, tied the unlucky fellow up securely.

The other man, seeing his companion knocked down by a woman, rushed over to help.

Ziyun met him with a strike of her stick, knocking him to the ground as well. Before Ziyun could even call out, the wives rushed forward and tied him up as well.

chapters.title: The First Glimmer of Talent
chapters.content:
Ziyun led the group of wives, escorting two Turkic spies to the camp headquarters. A messenger immediately reported to the commander: "Reporting to the Commander-in-Chief, seven or eight young wives have arrived at the gate, claiming they have captured spies sent by the Turks. They request an interrogation."

"Hmm? Such a thing actually happened? General Li, you go and see what this is all about." Commander Zhao could not be at the forefront of every matter, so he sent Deputy Commander General Li Hu to meet the young wives.

"Go, take those spies to my tent," Deputy Commander Li ordered the messenger.

"Understood!" The messenger went off to carry out the order.

When Deputy Commander Li entered his tent, he saw a group of young wives standing in a corner, guarding two men who were tightly bound.

Wei Ziyun was the leader among the wives. Deputy Commander Li thought to himself, "I knew she would be among them."

After sitting down in his large armchair, he asked, "What is going on here?"

"Reporting to the General," Ziyun stepped forward and said, "These two men have been wandering around our family quarters for quite a while. We found them suspicious and asked what they were doing. To our surprise, they drew their waist knives to attack me, so we subdued them and brought them here for you to interrogate."

"Good. There is nothing more for you to do here. Go to Commander Zhao’s tent and recount the whole process to him."

"Understood!" the wives replied, mimicking the tone of the soldiers, and left the tent.

"Ha! You two losers, you couldn't even beat our women! Why don't you confess everything now?"

After saying this, Deputy Commander Li pointed to the man standing in front and said, "You, stand forward. You first: where are you from, and what are you here for?"

"I am a Turk, and I will not say anything," the man in front replied, remaining stubborn.

"You won't talk? Fine. If you won't talk, take him out!"

Deputy Commander Li gave the order, and two guards dragged him away.

The remaining Turkic spy, thinking that Deputy Commander Li was going to have the other man beheaded, was so terrified that his legs went weak.

Seeing his expression, Deputy Commander Li knew he was a coward. He said to him, "If you don't say anything, your fate will be the same as his; the wolves will come to collect your bodies tonight. If you confess, I can spare your life. Will you talk or not?"

"Spare me, Commander! I will talk! I will tell you everything I know! Please, spare me. I don't want to die."

"Good. It’s good that you don't want to die. Answer whatever I ask you truthfully. If you hide anything, just wait for the wolves to come and collect your body!"

"Yes, I dare not hide anything."

"I ask you: what is your name? Who sent you? What are you here for?"

"Reporting to the Commander, my name is Suotu. I was sent by our Great Leader, Zhazage. The purpose was to spy on the strength and weaknesses of the Tang army. If we couldn't find that out, capturing a live prisoner to take back would also suffice. I never expected that instead of capturing a live person, we would be tied up by a few women."

"I ask you, how many cavalrymen do you have now?"

"Reporting to the Commander, I don't know the exact number; I haven't counted. However, I estimate there are about two thousand. The horses are all fine horses, and the blades are all sharp."

"Hmm." This matched the intelligence data Deputy Commander Li possessed, which meant the fellow hadn't dared to lie. He continued, "How far is your camp from ours?"

"Reporting to the Commander, not too far, not too close, about a hundred li."

This also matched the intelligence. He continued, "How many people are in your tribe now?"

"Reporting to the Commander, I haven't counted that, I really dare not say."

"I believe you haven't counted. I don't blame you. Do you know how many people are in your small tribes?"

"Reporting to the Commander, I know that. Each of our small tribes has over four thousand people, counting the elderly and children."

"How many tribes do you have in total?"

"Reporting to the Commander, I haven't counted that either. But I estimate there must be dozens. Every year, the Great Leader summons the leaders of each group to the main camp for a drink, and dozens of them come." This also matched the intelligence.

"How is your harvest this year?" This was the question Deputy Commander Li was most interested in.

If the Turkic harvest was good, they would live in peace and enjoy their blessings within the tribe; if the harvest was poor and they had nothing to eat or drink, they would invade the Tang borders and raid the border residents.

"Reporting to the Commander, we suffered a disaster last year!" This was intelligence Deputy Commander Li did not have, so he asked seriously, "What kind of disaster? Tell me slowly."

"Reporting to the Commander, there was a drought last year. It didn't rain for a long time. Most of the pastures didn't grow any grass, and many of our cattle and sheep starved to death."

"Hmm, so you are running out of food, right?"

"Reporting to the Commander, we’ve eaten everything we could. We can't kill all the cattle and sheep; what would we do if we killed them all?"

"So your Great Leader sent you to spy on our Tang army because you want to come and steal our cattle, sheep, and grain, right?" Deputy Commander Li asked calmly.

"Reporting to the Commander, I don't know about that. Our Great Leader didn't say."

"Hmm, your Great Leader wouldn't tell you that. I ask you, what do you do when you run out of food?"

"Reporting to the Commander, according to past customs, we come to the Tang border to raid."

"Hmm, it seems you didn't dare to fool me. I always keep my word; I won't kill you." After saying this, he told the messenger, "Take him away, keep him under strict guard, and don't let him escape."

"Understood!"

Inside Commander Zhao's tent, the Commander was chatting happily with Ziyun and the other wives.

Wei Ping was eloquent; she recounted the entire process of capturing the Turkic spies in great detail.

"Wife of Hui Guang, you know martial arts?" Commander Zhao was both surprised and delighted as he asked Ziyun.

"Reporting to the Commander," Ziyun said very modestly, "When I was young, I learned a few sets of self-defense techniques from my uncle."

Commander Zhao thought to himself, "A few sets of self-defense techniques were enough to knock Turkic men to the ground? These Turkic soldiers are no ordinary people." He asked, "What does your uncle do?"

"Reporting to the Commander," Ziyun continued in a low-key manner, "My uncle is the Chief Instructor of the Imperial Guard, Zhou."

As soon as Ziyun said this, Commander Zhao was stunned for a moment, muttering to himself, "So that's it." He immediately said to Ziyun, "I know a thing or two about Chief Instructor Zhou. Since you received his true teachings, your martial arts must be remarkable."

"I truly cannot underestimate this little palace maid." Thinking this, he said to the wives, "You not only have high vigilance but are also very brave. You have performed a great service. According to military regulations, you must be rewarded. Tell me, what do you want?"

"Are we really getting a reward?" Shuangshuang asked.

"There are no jokes in the military. Tell me what you want."

"Since it's a reward according to military regulations, let's just follow the regulations," Xiaohong chimed in.

"According to military regulations, for capturing two spies, the reward should be two large yellow sheep and two jars of aged wine. Do you want that?" Commander Zhao was afraid they might not like it.

"We do!" the young wives shouted in unison.

Commander Zhao laughed when he heard them say "We do!" These young wives were something else, asking for wine and sheep! He told the messenger, "Pass my order to the quartermaster: select the two fattest, largest yellow sheep and two jars of aged wine for them. Tell him this is a reward!"

"Understood!"

"You all go and collect your reward," Commander Zhao said to the wives.

"You go ahead, I have something to discuss with the Commander," Ziyun said to Wei Ping, Shuangshuang, and Xiaohong.

"Okay." The wives followed the messenger to collect their reward, leaving Ziyun alone in the tent.

"Wife of Hui Guang, what else is on your mind?" Commander Zhao asked cautiously, not knowing what this mysterious palace maid wanted.

"Reporting to the Commander," Ziyun said, "I would like to organize the young wives and form a Women's Self-Defense Corps."

At this moment, Deputy Commander Li, having finished interrogating the Turkic spy, entered Commander Zhao's tent. Hearing that Ziyun wanted to form a Women's Self-Defense Corps, he asked before he even sat down, "Can you women fight against Turkic soldiers? Don't think that just because you luckily captured two Turkic spies today, you are something special. Didn't you notice that those two Turkic spies didn't know martial arts?"

"Reporting to the Deputy Commander," Ziyun explained, "We won't be engaging in hand-to-hand combat with the Turks. We can stand guard and keep watch to discover enemy movements in advance. Our main purpose is to protect our homes and the safety of our families; we don't intend to go to the battlefield with the soldiers."

"If that is the case, it is worth considering." Deputy Commander Li sat down and looked at Commander Zhao, waiting for his decision.

"You young wives do need something to do. Otherwise, you'll just be idling at home and causing trouble. You may form a Women's Self-Defense Corps. Go ask Deputy Commander Li for equipment. However, you must follow one prohibition."

Ziyun looked at Commander Zhao and asked, "Reporting to the Commander, what prohibition?"

"You are only allowed to operate within the family quarters; you are not allowed to take a single step outside the compound."

Hearing the Commander say this, Deputy Commander Li almost laughed out loud. If they couldn't even leave the compound, what kind of "Self-Defense Corps" was that? Wasn't it the same as staying home and raising children? So, he immediately asked Ziyun, "What equipment do you need?"

Ziyun thought for a moment and said, "Reporting to the Deputy Commander, just equip each of us with a small waist knife and a crossbow. We will figure out the uniforms ourselves."

"That equipment is readily available. Whenever you have organized your team, go to the quartermaster to collect it."

"Understood! Thank you, Commander! Thank you, Deputy Commander!"

"Report..."

At this moment, a messenger came to report.

"Speak."

"Reporting to the Commander and Deputy Commander, the quartermaster has already issued the two fattest yellow sheep and two jars of aged wine to the wives."

"Good!" Commander Zhao said, then asked Ziyun, "Wife of Hui Guang, is there anything else?"

Ziyun shook her head and said, "Reporting to the Commander, nothing else."

"Then hurry home and stew your meat."

Ziyun left the Commander's tent and caught up with the wives who were carrying the wine and sheep.

After they returned, they gathered at Ziyun's house, borrowed a large pot from the kitchen, and stewed the sheep. Eating just mutton was too simple, so Ziyun asked the other wives, "Do you have any other food at home?"

"Yes! How could we live without food?" Wei Ping replied.

"If you have it, that's good. Go back and bring the food from your homes, and bring your tables, chairs, benches, bowls, and chopsticks. We'll make a few more dishes and wait for the men to come back tonight to eat meat and drink wine together."

"Okay!" The wives went off.

Before long, the courtyard was filled with tables, chairs, benches, bowls, and chopsticks from every household. Those who were thoughtful even brought two more pots and set them up in the courtyard to stir-fry dishes.

Every time Chen Huiguang went home to eat, "Skinny Monkey" would follow him to sponge off a meal. As they approached Chen Huiguang's house, Skinny Monkey suddenly said, "Brother, your house smells like stewed meat!"

"Are you hungry? We didn't go hunting, where would there be meat? Should I stew you? You don't have any meat on your bones anyway, who would want to gnaw on them?"

"My nose has never been wrong. Want to bet?"

"Bet it is!"

The two bet that whoever lost would not be allowed to drink wine or eat meat that night, and could only watch.

Chen Huiguang's courtyard was relatively large, with rammed-earth walls and a wooden gate. He pushed the gate open and was stunned!

There was a group of young wives in the courtyard, busy stewing mutton!

In the center of the courtyard, a large pot was supported by several large stones, and the fire was burning brightly. The mutton in the pot had been cooking for a while, and the fragrance drifted out of the courtyard, which was what Skinny Monkey had smelled.

Several young wives were cleaning the sheep offal, and others had set up two smaller pots to cook other dishes. It looked like they were going to have a big feast tonight. Chen Huiguang and Skinny Monkey didn't know about the reward the wives had received and were momentarily bewildered.

"What are you standing there for? Come and give us a hand!" Xiaohong saw the two of them staring blankly at the gate and shouted at them. She was drawing water from the well in the courtyard.

Chen Huiguang owed his ability to have this courtyard to Ziyun. Without the Emperor's blessing and reward, a common soldier like him wouldn't even be able to get a wife, let alone such a large courtyard.

This courtyard was originally built for generals, and since the serving generals all had housing, it had been sitting empty.

When Ziyun married him, Chen Huiguang was just a common soldier with no place to live. But how could he marry a palace maid bestowed by the Emperor without a bridal chamber?

After Guo Ziyi consulted with General Zhao Shan, they gave this courtyard to Chen Huiguang. A palace maid from the imperial palace had to live in better conditions. Otherwise, if the Emperor were to ask, and Guo Ziyi and General Zhao Shan hadn't even provided them with housing, it would have been a huge problem.

The best thing about this courtyard was the well, which made using water very convenient. There were also several large tiled rooms, making it spacious. It was very suitable for them to cook and dine here.

"What's going on?" Chen Huiguang asked Xiaohong. He didn't see his wife; Ziyun was busy inside the house and hadn't seen him return.

"You don't know? Today we captured two Turkic spies, and the Commander rewarded us with two yellow sheep and two jars of aged wine. Your place is spacious, and since you have no elderly or children, it's convenient for everything, so we decided to have our gathering at your house."

"Is that so?" Chen Huiguang couldn't feel happy upon hearing this news. He had lost the bet; he couldn't eat meat or drink wine, what bad luck!

At this moment, Skinny Monkey also came over to help draw water and whispered to Chen Huiguang, "We'll settle the bet later. Today's situation is special; you can drink and eat meat."

"Now that's a real brother!" Chen Huiguang patted Skinny Monkey on the shoulder.

"Did you young wives really capture two Turkic spies?" Skinny Monkey didn't believe it and asked Xiaohong.

"Don't believe it? You'll believe it after you eat the meat and drink the wine in a while." Xiaohong knew that it wasn't just the two of them who didn't believe it; many people wouldn't. She didn't want to explain further, the General's reward was right there; believe it or not, it was the truth.

Ziyun came out of the house and saw Chen Huiguang and Skinny Monkey. Knowing the men had returned, she said to the wives, "Call your husbands and the elderly and young from your homes to come and eat meat and drink wine."

"Alright, I'm going."

"Me too." Two young wives excitedly went to call their families.

"Wait," Ziyun called them back and said, "Bring the steamed buns you have at home too. Whoever doesn't bring any won't get meat or wine." It was truly impossible to make enough staple food for so many people at Ziyun's house.

"Understood!" The two turned and left, mimicking the soldiers' tone.

Skinny Monkey saw that the large pot was filled with mutton, and other wives were stir-frying dishes in the courtyard. It looked like a very sumptuous feast, and he couldn't have been happier.

Soldiers in the barracks rarely got to eat delicacies, and they were all starved for good food. Seeing such a feast, they were drooling.

"Brother Guang, coming home with you this time was the right choice, meat to eat and wine to drink. From now on, I'm sticking with you! Wherever you go, I go!" Skinny Monkey, who had no strong opinions of his own, had always followed Chen Huiguang.

"Stop talking nonsense, help with the work, keep your eyes peeled, and you won't go hungry or thirsty!"

Chen Huiguang couldn't figure out how these young wives had subdued two Turkic spies. Turkic women were fierce, and the men were even more formidable. There must be more to this, and he suspected it had something to do with his wife.

Although Chen Huiguang had married Wei Ziyun, he knew very little about her background. Ziyun never spoke of it, and he knew nothing. He had never imagined that Ziyun knew martial arts. When they were together, they had never discussed such topics, who would have thought she knew how to fight?

Although he and Skinny Monkey had many questions, there was no opportunity to ask now. They had to help with the work and wait to eat meat and drink wine. Everything else was secondary; only the wine and meat were real!

Before long, everyone who was supposed to come had arrived. They brought more tables, chairs, and tableware, along with dishes and buns from their own homes, filling Chen Huiguang's courtyard to the brim.

chapters.title: Establishing the Women's Self-Defense Force
chapters.content:
Dishes and wine were laid out on the tables, and everyone was ready to feast. Xiao Hong said to Ziyun, "Wife of Huiguang, why don't you say a few words so we can start the banquet?"

"Very well, I will say a few words." Ziyun saw that everyone was looking at her with anticipation; she knew they were waiting for her to finish quickly so they could start eating.

"Today, a few of us wives caught two Turkic spies in the courtyard. Commander Zhao has rewarded us with two yellow sheep and two jars of aged wine. Some may find it hard to believe, but whether you believe it or not, we can discuss that after we've eaten and drunk. Without further ado, everyone, help yourselves to the meat and wine!"

The crowd applauded.

"Let the feast begin!"

The wives who had participated in catching the spies each brought a bowl of wine to toast Ziyun. Shuangshuang said, "Wife of Huiguang, if it weren't for you today, we wouldn't have been able to catch those two spies, nor would we have had meat to eat or wine to drink. We toast you!"

After Ziyun drank heartily with these wives, she set down her bowl and asked them, "The Commander has already agreed to let us establish a Women's Self-Defense Force. Are you willing to join?"

"I'm willing. As long as I'm with you, I'm willing to do anything," said Shuangshuang.

Xiao Hong immediately added, "I'm willing, too."

The other wives, however, were looking at their husbands; they could not make decisions on their own and needed their husbands' approval. Ziyun realized that if their husbands did not agree, they would not dare to join the Women's Self-Defense Force.

She picked up her wine bowl and said to everyone present, "Let us all drink a bowl together!"

Everyone raised their bowls, and someone shouted, "Bottoms up!"

After everyone had finished their wine, Ziyun said, "You all continue eating while I talk; we can do both at the same time."

"Good!" shouted Skinny Monkey, cheering for Huiguang's wife.

Ziyun continued, "Catching the two Turkic spies today was an accident, but also a coincidence. If it hadn't been for De Shun's wife discovering those spies early, not only would we not be here eating meat and drinking wine, but we would have lost someone, someone who likely would have already been dragged into the Turkic camp."

This was something no one had known or even considered.

Li Deshun was very concerned about this and asked, "What exactly happened? Can you tell us the sequence of events from today?"

"Certainly. De Shun's wife, please tell everyone what happened today." Ziyun nodded at Wei Ping.

Wei Ping, who loved excitement and enjoyed speaking and showing off, stood up immediately and recounted the events of the day in vivid and meticulous detail.

Chen Huiguang listened and broke into a cold sweat for his wife. He was now convinced that this wife from the palace not only knew martial arts but was highly skilled! He had to re-evaluate his wife.

After hearing his wife's description, Li Deshun felt that the family quarters were a blind spot in the camp's defense. He immediately said, "Our family quarters have never had any defenses. This is a loophole, and it must be plugged."

"Brother Li is right. The purpose of establishing the Women's Self-Defense Force is to plug this loophole. We will organize the young wives and girls to stand guard in the courtyard. If we discover enemy activity, we can report it to the main camp in time, preventing any surprise attacks. I hope you will support us," Ziyun said, building on Li Deshun's point.

"I support it!" Li Deshun was the first to declare.

"I support it too!"

"And I!" All the men present expressed their support.

"Thank you! Let's drink!" Ziyun held her bowl high.

"Bottoms up!" Skinny Monkey shouted again.

"Bottoms up!" Ziyun finished her wine first, and everyone followed suit. The matter was settled.

With the men's support for the Women's Self-Defense Force, Ziyun felt at ease. Without their support, this would never have succeeded.

"If there is a battle, will your Women's Self-Defense Force go to the front lines?" The man who asked this was Jiang Erwang, Xiao Hong's husband and a centurion.

"Brother Jiang, you can set your heart at ease. The Commander has given us a strict order: our Women's Self-Defense Force is only allowed to operate within the courtyard and is not permitted to step even half a step outside. Do you think we could go to the battlefield?" Ziyun asked in return.

"Hmm, that puts my mind at ease."

The other men, hearing Ziyun's words, also felt relieved. As long as they only operated within the courtyard, their safety was guaranteed.

The Turks either attacked the Great Tang's army directly or went to plunder the border people; they rarely attacked the families of the Tang army.

The reason was simple: these families were not wealthy, and there was nothing in their homes worth stealing. If not for the cloth and cotton Ziyun had donated, even their winter clothing would have been a problem.

Jiang Erwang, while gnawing on a sheep bone, asked Xiao Hong, "Did you really catch two Turkic spies? How come I never noticed you had such skills?"

"If you didn't notice, it's because you're blind! What are you gnawing on? What are you drinking? Did it fall from the sky? If you don't believe it, stop eating!" Xiao Hong said, reaching out to grab the large bone from his hand.

Jiang Erwang dodged and said, "I believe you, I believe you, isn't that enough?"

The situation at the other tables was much the same. It wasn't just the men who didn't believe these young wives had caught two Turkic spies; the elders didn't either. But with the real meat in their mouths and the aged wine in their bellies, they had no choice but to believe.

Two large, fat sheep, plus the vegetables brought from each household, were quite a lot, but they were no match for the large crowd and their appetites. Soon, the plates were empty, and the wine was gone. Ziyun asked everyone, "Are you full?"

"We're full!" everyone answered in unison, some burping and looking tipsy.

"In the future, if we receive more rewards, shall we gather here again?" Ziyun asked.

"Yes!"

"There is no banquet that doesn't end. Let's stop here for today. Everyone, take back the things you brought from home. Wives, please stay; we have something to discuss." Ziyun wanted to talk to them about the Women's Self-Defense Force.

The men didn't have much to say, and the wives felt a sense of pride in front of their husbands today. After everyone left, Chen Huiguang and Skinny Monkey cleaned up the courtyard, and Ziyun gathered the wives for a meeting.

"From now on, you are the backbone of our Women's Self-Defense Force. When you go back, explain the requirements for joining to the wives and girls who are interested. Starting tomorrow, they can come to me to sign up. Do you have any difficulties with this?"

"What's difficult about that?" Wei Ping said dismissively. "Today's events have already spread throughout the courtyard. Tomorrow, we won't even need to say anything; many people will surely come to ask us. By then, if I tell them about the Women's Self-Defense Force, the effect will surely be excellent."

"Such a big thing happened in our courtyard, and the main reason is that we received real rewards. Who in the courtyard isn't jealous? The scent of this meat and wine has already drifted into their homes. Wei Ping is right; we don't need to say much, they will definitely come to ask us," Xiao Hong added.

"Very well, let's see how many sign up tomorrow. I'll be waiting at home. Everyone worked hard today, go back and rest early. Dismissed."

The next day, there were indeed many people who came to sign up for the Women's Self-Defense Force. Ziyun limited the age to between eighteen and thirty. Those with many children, those who were nursing, those with elderly to care for, or those in poor health were not accepted.

In the end, Ziyun selected sixty women from over a hundred applicants, and the first Women's Self-Defense Force of Mucu Mountain was established. This force would later continue to grow and develop, becoming a "women's army" guarding the border, a highly combat-effective force. Of course, that is a story for another time.

Ziyun divided the sixty women into three squads of twenty each, appointing Wei Ping, Shuangshuang, and Xiao Hong as squad leaders.

They received small waist swords and crossbows from the quartermaster, with each crossbow equipped with two hundred arrows, and each person received a set.

With weapons, they still lacked cotton combat robes. No household had enough cloth or cotton to make one. The five hundred bolts of cloth and one hundred piculs of cotton Ziyun had donated had all been used up by the families.

Ziyun took out a pair of jade bracelets given to her by the Imperial Concubine and said to the three squad leaders, "Come, let's go to town and pawn them for some silver."

"But this is part of the dowry the Imperial Concubine gave you!" Wei Ping couldn't bear to see Ziyun pawn her dowry.

"Can't we think of another way?" Xiao Hong also didn't want Ziyun to pawn her dowry.

"Do we have any other good way?" Ziyun asked them.

All three shook their heads at the same time; their families would be lucky to scrape together a few hundred copper coins.

"It's alright. It won't be long before I redeem them. Trust me." Ziyun was very confident; she didn't view these treasures as that important.

However, she regarded everything the Imperial Concubine had given her as a treasure; if not for the Women's Self-Defense Force, she would never have pawned them.

"How much do you plan to pawn them for?" Shuangshuang asked.

The currency used in the Great Tang Empire was copper coins, but their gold content was too low to buy much.

"We have sixty female soldiers. Each needs a cotton combat robe, a hat, and a pair of cotton boots. And the four of us, don't we each need a warhorse?" Ziyun asked.

"Won't Commander Zhao issue these to us?" Wei Ping asked.

"It's good enough that he agreed to let us establish the Women's Self-Defense Force. Besides, there's nothing in his supply depot. Didn't you visit the depot when you went to collect the swords and crossbows? What was in there? We have to rely on ourselves."

"Sigh, our border garrison has always been poor; the military supplies allocated by the Emperor are too little." Xiao Hong and everyone else knew the border defense forces were poor.

"To buy all these things, we'd need several large baskets of copper coins; we couldn't carry them," Wei Ping said. After marrying into a large family, she had become the household manager and was responsible for procurement, so she knew the market well.

"Can't we exchange the copper coins for gold or silver? Pawn tickets can also be used as money," Shuangshuang said, having pawned items before and knowing that pawn tickets could be used like cash.

"Then let's pawn them for more silver. We need silver to buy horses, cloth, and cotton." Wei Ping understood Ziyun's intention: to get the Women's Self-Defense Force up and running, money was essential.

At that time in the Tang Dynasty, there were no silver banknotes. Copper coins were fine for small items, but for large transactions, they were impractical. Gold and silver were the primary currencies for large deals.

"How much silver do you estimate this pair of jade bracelets can be pawned for?" Ziyun asked.

"Five thousand taels," Shuangshuang blurted out.

"These are treasures bestowed by the Imperial Concubine; they must be worth at least ten thousand!" Xiao Hong knew the value of the jade bracelets.

"We won't pawn them for that much. Just one thousand taels. After buying the cloth, cotton, and horses, we'll keep the rest for our daily expenses." Ziyun had long-term plans.

"One thousand taels? That much silver? How will we redeem them later?" Shuangshuang was worried about whether they could ever redeem the jade bracelets, as they had no way to earn money.

"We'll deal with the future when it comes. There will be a way when we reach the mountain!" Ziyun believed she would definitely be able to redeem the bracelets.

Ziyun wrapped the jade bracelets in a piece of silk, tucked a small waist sword she had brought from the palace into her belt, and said to the three squad leaders, "We're going shopping today."

The four women arrived at the busiest street in Taiping Town and soon found the largest pawnshop. Ziyun was about to step inside when Wei Ping pulled her back and said, "You and Xiao Hong go in. Shuangshuang and I will stay outside. Pawnshop owners are all black-hearted wolves; be careful they don't swindle your treasure. If we have people inside and outside, we can prevent any accidents."

Ziyun felt Wei Ping's reasoning was sound, so she and Xiao Hong entered the pawnshop.

The counter was very high. Ziyun unwrapped the silk and said to the clerk inside, "I want to pawn this for one thousand taels."

The clerk at the counter was young and couldn't make a decision on such a large sum of silver, so he said to Ziyun, "Young lady, please wait a moment. I will call our manager."

An old man, about fifty years old, soon entered. His temples were slightly gray, his hair was neatly combed, and he had the air of a boss.

He sat down, took one look at the jade bracelets, paused for a moment, then looked at Ziyun and Xiao Hong and asked, "Are these your bracelets?"

"Yes," Ziyun replied.

"How much silver do you want? A dead pawn or a live pawn?"

"One thousand taels, a live pawn."

After hearing this, the boss whispered a few words to the clerk, who immediately left. He then said to Ziyun and Xiao Hong, "You two wait a moment; I'll have someone fetch the silver."

"Fetch the silver? Can't we use a pawn ticket?" Xiao Hong asked.

"You know your stuff. A one-thousand-tael pawn ticket is not a small amount. Please wait a moment." After saying this, the manager even smiled at Ziyun and Xiao Hong.

Suddenly, several burly men entered, surrounded Ziyun and Xiao Hong, and locked the front door.

Before Ziyun could react, Xiao Hong was pinned down by a large man, who said to Ziyun, "Hand over your waist sword, or she'll suffer."

Seeing that Xiao Hong was pinned, Ziyun feared they would hurt her, so she handed over her sword and asked, "What do you want?"

The manager sneered, "Bold thieves! Where did you get these jade bracelets? Confess, or we'll send you to the authorities!"

Ziyun had initially thought they were after her money and life, but hearing the manager, she realized it was a misunderstanding.

"Let's talk this over. Let her go. There are so many of you; two young women like us can't run away," Ziyun said, stepping aside.

The manager signaled the man to release Xiao Hong and then said, "Speak. Where did these jade bracelets come from?"

Outside, Shuangshuang and Wei Ping saw what was happening in the pawnshop and pounded on the door. "Open up! It's broad daylight; what is the meaning of locking the door?"

The clerk came out and said, "We lost something in the shop and are searching for it. It's not convenient to open the door. Please go to another pawnshop for your business."

Wei Ping immediately realized that these people wanted to steal Ziyun's jade bracelets, and with their four-person skill set, they were no match for those men. She said to Shuangshuang, "Let's go."

The two walked aside, and the clerk immediately locked the door tight.

"You stay here and keep watch. I'm going back to report this," Wei Ping said and left.

Shuangshuang hid at a distance, keeping her eyes fixed on the pawnshop door.

Wei Ping often came here for supplies and knew many people. She immediately borrowed a fast horse and rode back to report.

After hearing Wei Ping's report, Commander Zhao immediately ordered a messenger to take Wei Ping to find Chen Huiguang. He told Chen Huiguang to take a small squad of cavalry to follow Wei Ping to the pawnshop, but instructed them not to act rashly until the truth was known.

When Chen Huiguang heard his wife was being held at the pawnshop, he was frantic. He immediately gathered his men and set off, saying to Wei Ping, "Lead the way, quickly! Everyone, follow!"

Chen Huiguang caught up to Wei Ping's horse and asked, "Why would the people at the pawnshop detain them?"

"The clerk said they lost something. I suspect they want to steal your wife's jade bracelets."

"You went to pawn something?"

"You didn't know?"

"I didn't." Chen Huiguang truly didn't know; Ziyun hadn't told him about it.

By the time Wei Ping finished briefly explaining what happened, they had already arrived at the entrance of the pawnshop.

chapters.title: Well-Trained
chapters.content:
Seeing Wei Ping arrive with people, Shuangshuang went up to meet them and said, "The main gate has been closed the whole time, and we haven't noticed any movement."

Chen Huiguang jumped off his warhorse and went to knock on the door, which opened immediately.

Inside, Ziyun and Xiaohong were sitting in the front hall of the pawnshop with two chests placed on the floor. Chen Huiguang stepped forward and asked Ziyun, "Are you both alright?"

"We're fine. Why are you here?"

"I came to see if I could be of any help."

"Perfect. You can help move these two chests out to the cart waiting at the door."

As they exited the pawnshop, the manager and his assistants came to see them off.

"I have eyes but failed to recognize a person of importance; please forgive my earlier offense, young lady," the manager said, his face full of smiles as he apologetically escorted Ziyun and the others outside.

A carriage was already waiting. The manager said to Ziyun, "Since you have purchased so many items, please borrow this carriage. Whenever you are finished with it, just have the driver bring it back."

Turning to the driver, he instructed, "From now on, you are to drive for this young lady. You must follow her orders without fail!"

"Thank you! You may return now; we are leaving."

After saying this, Ziyun told the driver, "We are going to the fabric store."

Ziyun and the three young wives boarded the carriage, with Chen Huiguang’s cavalry squad following behind. The pawnshop manager and his assistants gasped at the sight.

"Good thing we didn't treat them rudely, otherwise the consequences would have been unthinkable," the manager muttered to himself. In any dynasty, the military's fist is always the hardest.

In the carriage, Wei Ping asked Ziyun, "What happened? You scared me to death earlier. What were you..."

"Haha, let me tell you," Xiaohong said with a laugh. "At first, they took us for thieves, thinking we were maids from a wealthy family who had stolen a jade bracelet to pawn. The manager said commoners wouldn't have such precious jade. Several burly men came over, pinned me down, and started interrogating Huiguang's wife."

"Did they hit you?" Shuangshuang asked.

"No. Before they were sure of our identities, they didn't dare do anything to us."

"Then how did they believe you weren't thieves?" Shuangshuang asked again.

"Huiguang's wife asked them one question, and they believed her."

"What question?"

"She asked if they had heard about a palace maid who married into Muci Mountain. They said they had. Then she told them to look at her waist saber before speaking further."

"Right, her waist saber was brought out from the palace; it's different from ours," Shuangshuang realized.

"Once the manager saw the exquisite craftsmanship of her saber and the ruby embedded in the hilt, his attitude changed instantly. He smiled obsequiously, told us it was a misunderstanding, and sent the burly men away. Then he served us tea and was extremely polite."

"Phew, a false alarm."

"You should head back, otherwise Commander Zhao might think something happened to us," Ziyun said to Chen Huiguang.

"Alright, I'll go report to the Commander and leave two cavalrymen to help you move your things." With that, he left two men behind and returned with his squad.

The shopping went smoothly. Fabric, cotton, needles and thread, and four warhorses were all purchased, with one hundred taels of silver remaining for the daily expenses of the Women's Self-Defense Force.

The Women's Self-Defense Force was a civilian-run organization without imperial funding. The women trained and stood guard as volunteers, and no one provided their meals.

They all ate at home, and working for the force inevitably led to complaints from their families. Therefore, solving the food issue was crucial for the development of the force. This could not be done by Ziyun's donations alone; another way had to be found.

However, if this force wasn't built up, it wouldn't be long before it fell apart. The primary issue facing the Women's Self-Defense Force was to gain recognition as an official military unit.

Ziyun went to Commander Zhao's main tent. "Wei Ziyun, Captain of the Muci Mountain Women's Self-Defense Force, pays her respects to the Commander."

"No need for formalities. What brings you here?" Commander Zhao had been impressed by her after hearing she had pawned the pair of jade bracelets gifted by the Imperial Concubine to provide winter bedding and horses for the women.

"Reporting to the Commander, the weapons training for the Women's Self-Defense Force has begun. I request that you assign us a crossbow instructor!"

"Is that all?"

"Reporting to the Commander, that is all."

"Granted. I will assign you the best crossbow instructor in the entire camp immediately. Anything else?"

"Reporting to the Commander, nothing else. Thank you, Commander!"

When it came to weapons and instructors, Commander Zhao had them, and he supported the women's force with everything he had. But as for food and drink, he didn't even have enough for the men, so he was powerless there.

When Ziyun returned, the crossbow instructor had arrived. His name was Yan Youyan, a man in his forties who was a gold-medal archer, famous throughout the camp.

Ziyun scheduled six hours of crossbow training daily, three in the morning and three in the afternoon. Starting from the basics, she trained every woman strictly.

Before every training session, she would tell them: "We women lack the brute strength of men; we are no match for Turkic soldiers in hand-to-hand combat. Therefore, we must shoot them down from thirty paces away. We cannot let them get close!"

Yan Youyan lived up to his name; he was strict. He trained the women with the same meticulousness as the men. They practiced the simple motion of raising the crossbow and nocking an arrow thousands of times until every woman’s movement was as standard as a soldier's.

During training, Yan noticed that the women generally lacked wrist strength, making it difficult to pull the bowstring and slowing down the arrow-nocking process. On the battlefield, this was a fatal weakness.

In battle, cavalry charges are fast; if you haven't nocked your arrow, the enemy is already upon you.

Ziyun called on everyone to brainstorm a solution.

The first phase of basic training lasted ten days. The assessment was to hit a fixed half-body target at fifty paces. Under Instructor Yan's personal evaluation, all sixty women passed.

After the assessment, Instructor Yan said only one sentence, which brought great satisfaction to the women: "You young wives are teachable!"

The second phase focused on the speed of nocking arrows and pulling the string. Yan’s requirement was: when he shouted "One," they had to have the arrow nocked and the target aimed, ready to fire.

Many women lacked the strength to pull the string easily, making them slow. Ziyun and Yan tried many methods, but with little success.

Progress stalled. Just as they were at their wit's end, a beautiful woman named Jin Taoye approached Ziyun with her crossbow. "Captain, my husband made this for me. It's very easy to use and saves a lot of effort."

Ziyun looked and saw a hemp rope fixed to the crossbow handle. The rope looped around the bowstring; by pulling the rope back, the string was drawn onto the trigger mechanism, then the arrow was nocked, ready to fire.

Ziyun tried it a few times and found it very efficient. She asked, "What does your husband do?"

"He is a centurion in the Third Garrison, named Ji Donglai. He comes from a family of carpenters and is very skilled."

"Good! Your husband has solved a major problem for our force. I will reward him with a jar of wine! This method can be promoted throughout the team. Let's go find Instructor Yan."

After testing Taoye's crossbow, the instructor said to them, "Excellent! After each shot, pull the rope back, and the string is set. It’s fast and effortless. We will implement this for the whole team."

That day, every crossbow in the Women's Self-Defense Force was fitted with a sturdy hemp rope, and a new round of training began.

At the end of this phase, when Yan tested their speed, he was shocked: before he could even shout "Two," the women had already nocked their arrows and were ready to fire.

A smile appeared on the instructor's face.

He told Ziyun, "At this speed, you can fire three to four times within a hundred paces. Turkic cavalry are fast, but they aren't faster than your arrows! I feel a great sense of accomplishment!"

The third phase was shooting at fixed full-body targets at one hundred paces, requiring perfect accuracy. The fourth phase was moving targets at one hundred paces, requiring at least four shots before the target reached twenty paces. The fifth phase was precision shooting, starting with potato targets and moving to hawthorn berries.

During the assessment, they hung ten hawthorn berries on threads at one hundred paces. Hitting six was passing, seven was good, and eight or more was excellent.

The results for the sixty women were: 60 passed, 36 good, and 18 excellent. This performance was far better than the men's.

Instructor Yan had initially agreed to be the instructor out of curiosity, not expecting much. But now, he had to admit that women had an advantage in archery, with higher precision than men.

Having trained men for over a decade, this conclusion was unexpected even to him. He was certain that if they went to the battlefield, as long as they had enough arrows, the enemy would never get close to them.

The sixth phase was shooting at moving targets: horizontal and vertical.

Horizontal movement was easy for them; they just had to lead the target. But vertical movement was difficult. The speed of a charging warhorse put immense psychological pressure on the women, and many felt fear.

To overcome this, Instructor Yan personally rode as the target, letting the women shoot with blunt arrows. After repeating this for over ten days, every woman adapted to the realistic battlefield environment and passed.

The final assessment: he charged at full speed from one hundred paces. By the time he reached twenty paces, he was hit by at least three and at most five arrows.

With such speed and precision, Yan was convinced no cavalry could break their lines.

After the training, Yan reported the results to Commander Zhao. The Commander just laughed and said, "If we send young wives to the battlefield, the enemy will laugh at us men. But it's fine. You're impressive for turning these young women into soldiers."

Yan knew the Commander looked down on them, just as he once had. But now, they had changed his perspective. He suddenly had an idea: he wanted to train them into a elite crossbow unit. If needed, they could deal the enemy an unexpected blow; there had been many such "women's armies" in history.

Thinking this, he said to Commander Zhao, "The task you gave me is complete. I won't play with these young wives anymore."

He said this because he wanted to stay. He knew the Commander's temperament well: the more you want to do something, the more he forbids it; the more you don't want to do something, the more he insists.

"What? Bored after only half a year? This Wei Ziyun was sent here by the Emperor; we cannot neglect her."

"Since there are no new recruits and few training tasks in the garrisons, you continue training these young women. When you think they're ready, we'll hold a shooting competition between the men and women to liven things up and boost the men's morale. What do you think?"

"Reporting to the Commander," Yan said, "since you put it that way, I will obey."

Yan returned and relayed the news to Ziyun and the three squad leaders.

"A competition against us?" Wei Ping asked.

"That's the idea. Do you dare?" Yan asked.

"We do!" the three squad leaders replied without hesitation.

"Hehe," Ziyun laughed, "if the men compete against the women in crossbow shooting, the men have no chance of winning."

"How so?" Yan asked, puzzled.

"If the women lose, people will say it's expected because men are stronger. If it's a draw, people will laugh at the men for being slow. If the women win, people will laugh at the men even more," Ziyun explained.

"So, it doesn't matter if we lose, right?" Shuangshuang asked.

"Yes," Ziyun said. "So when we compete, everyone should relax. I believe we won't lose to the men."

"I'm confident in crossbow shooting, but what about hand-to-hand combat?" Wei Ping asked.

"They won't make you fight hand-to-hand," Yan said. "We will only compete in crossbows. From now on, I will intensify your training. Don't be afraid of hardship. The more you suffer now, the better your chances of winning, and the less blood will be shed in battle. Understand?"

"Understood!" the three squad leaders replied in unison.

And so, a new round of training began.

This phase focused on actual combat, primarily improving the women's psychological resilience. Their technical skills were already perfected.

On the battlefield, psychological resilience is crucial. "When two armies meet, the brave win." It is a battle of nerves.

Yan knew that in the bloody chaos of war, what captures a soldier's soul is the command. So, he made commands the focus of this phase.

He told the sixty women: "Commands are your soul. Every one of you must obey them unconditionally!"

He took out a bamboo whistle and blew it loudly. "Can everyone hear this?"

"Yes!" they all replied.

"Good. This whistle is our command. No matter who blows it, at the first sound, you must draw your crossbow and an arrow and nock it immediately. This motion must be fluid, without pause."

"Do not look down at your arrow or crossbow. Rely entirely on feeling. Your eyes must stay on the enemy! Do you understand?"

"Understood!"

"This motion requires eight days of practice. Begin!"
